components.name: Dictionary
components.desc: Looks words up in the installed dictionaries, keeps glosses and searches.

components.name: Dictionary entry
components.desc: The right-hand pane that shows the dictionary entries for a tapped or searched word: the form, its possible lemmata and readings, and one fold-out section per dictionary.
components.detail: `renderView` draws the page for the current view (`S.view`): it asks the analysis for the lemmata of the form, picks the reading of the text's token if the word came from the text, then fetches the entries of every switched-on dictionary of that language (`entriesFor`) and renders them. Afterwards it makes words tappable, paints the highlights, fills the gloss box and restores the scroll position. Everything comes from the dictionaries stored in IndexedDB, so it works offline.

mem: est. 1-5 MB: the rendered entries (a long LSJ/Georges entry can be 100+ KB of HTML) plus the analysis' bucket cache
store: code; reads dictionary databases and a few settings keys
cpu: per word shown: entry lookup, HTML build, tree walks to wrap words

components.name: Entry formatting & cross-references
components.desc: Turns a stored dictionary entry into displayable HTML, explains the editors' colour codes, and appends entries it refers to ('→ see: …').
components.detail: `renderEntryHTML` adds a headword line unless the entry has its own, and follows the entry's references (`e.r`) up to three levels deep via `entryByRef`, skipping entries already shown. `normalizeHTML` replaces the old `<font color>` tags of the Eulexis data (Pape, LSJ) by spans whose tooltip tells the meaning from `FONT_MEANING` (author, variant, hapax, doubtful reading …). `FONT_MEANING` is also used by the Dictionaries dialog.

mem: the HTML strings of one word's entries
cpu: regex replace and recursion per entry

components.name: Open/closed dictionary sections
components.desc: Remembers, per lemma, which dictionary sections the reader opened or closed differently from the default.
components.detail: `saveOpenState` stores only the sections whose state differs from the default list `S.dictPrefs.open`, under the settings key `open|<lemma key>` (removed when nothing differs). `renderView` reads it back; an older format (a plain list) is still understood.

store: one small settings record per lemma touched, in IndexedDB 'greekreader'

components.name: Entry page
components.desc: Builds the entry page: the form (with vowel lengths for Latin), chips for each possible lemma, buttons for each grammatical reading, and the dictionary sections.
components.detail: `renderView` is the central function: it gets `analyses(form)`, chooses the lemma (explicit choice, the token's lemma, or the analysis' pick), shows the readings of the token with the shared part of the grammar labels written once in front, then loops over `S.shown` dictionaries of the language. A dictionary without its own entry but with a 'discussed under' pointer (`#m`) shows those entries instead. Sections are `<details>` that open according to the user's preferences or the remembered per-lemma state. It also handles the 'no dictionaries installed' and 'all switched off' hints and hands search views to `renderSearch`.

mem: est. 1-5 MB DOM of the entries shown
cpu: once per word: several IndexedDB reads, string building, DOM insert; awaits each entry in turn

components.name: Scroll memory
components.desc: Returns the dictionary pane to where the reader had scrolled: per tapped word of a text, otherwise per lemma.
components.detail: `wireDictScroll` listens to scrolling of the pane (ignoring tab switches and redraws) and `flushDictScroll` writes the position 300 ms after scrolling stops to the settings key from `scrollKey` (`sc|<text>|<token>` or `sc|@<lemma>`). The position is only restored when it belongs to the same lemma. The Lemmata list keeps its own scroll position in memory.

store: one small settings record per word looked up in a text (grows over time; est. well under 1 MB)

components.name: Tappable words in entries
components.desc: Makes Greek words, and the Latin words of Latin entries, inside dictionary entries tappable so the reader can jump to their entries.
components.detail: `wrapGreek` walks every text node and wraps each Greek token (2+ Greek letters) in a `.gw` span. `wrapLatin` is subtler because Georges and Lewis & Short mix German/English with Latin: it cuts each line at punctuation into stretches and links words only in stretches where at least 60% of the words are recognised by the Latin morphology (`latAnalyze`), skipping abbreviations, authors, references and a stop list of common German/English words (`NOT_LATIN`); cross-references after 'v.', 's.', 'cf.' or '=' are always linked. Results are memoised per word for one entry page.

mem: a per-page memo of recognised Latin words
cpu: Latin entries: a morphological analysis per distinct word of long entries (est. tens of ms to ~1 s for very long Georges entries); Greek: one regex pass

components.name: Glosses: data, export and reattaching
components.desc: What each gloss (a note on words of a text) remembers, exporting all glosses, and finding glosses a new place when their text changed or was removed.
components.detail: A gloss is stored in IndexedDB 'greekreader' (store `glosses`) with its text id and first/last word; this module adds the glossed words, lemma, reference, five words of context on each side and the text's title/author, so glosses can be exported meaningfully and reattached later. Reattaching matches the stored word and context against a text and lets the user approve each match.

mem: est. a few MB while matching: the words of the candidate texts
store: gloss records grow by the stored context (est. ~200-400 bytes per gloss)
cpu: matching and migration run on the main thread, yielding between glosses / texts

components.name: Glosses document (HTML / Word)
components.desc: Lays out the readable glosses document: title, headings per text or lemma, each gloss with its reference and context.
components.detail: `glossDocHTML` with `GLOSS_CSS` gives the HTML used for printing and the HTML file; `glossDocx` writes the same as WordprocessingML paragraphs with `wP`/`wRun` and packs a minimal .docx with `zipFiles`. (The inventory's 'top level' entry of glosses.js is the XML text inside `glossDocx`.)

components.name: Glosses export dialog
components.desc: Exports all glosses or those of one text as CSV, PDF, HTML or Word, in reading order or by lemma, optionally with the default glosses.
components.detail: `glossExportDialog` (opened from ☰ → This Pult → Annotations) first completes older glosses (`glossMigrate`), collects and sorts the glosses, and builds either a CSV (Text, Reference, Word, Lemma, Gloss, Context, Date) or a document grouped by text or lemma. PDF goes through the print dialog; HTML embeds the fonts (`fontFacesInline`); Word uses `glossDocx`. `glossSave` offers the file as a tap-to-save link (revoked after 60 s).

mem: all gloss records plus the file in memory (est. <5 MB; HTML adds ~0.8 MB of embedded fonts)

components.name: Finding a gloss's place
components.desc: Looks for a gloss in a text by its word and the five words on each side, tolerating accents, small spelling changes and edits nearby.
components.detail: Words are compared accent- and case-free (`glFold`). `glFind` tries every position where the glossed word(s) occur and scores the context with a longest-common-subsequence (`glLcs`) over the 10 surrounding words; at least 7 of 10 must match, or 9 of 10 if the word itself differs by up to two letters (`glEdit`). The best score wins, ties go to the position nearest the old one; a match is 'certain' when exact with 9-10 of 10. `glMatch` runs this over candidate texts, yielding after each gloss.

cpu: per gloss: a scan of all words of each text, small DP tables per candidate

components.name: Gloss context
components.desc: Stores with each gloss its words, lemma, reference, surrounding words and the text's title, and fills them in for older glosses.
components.detail: `glossSource` provides the words, references and a lemma function for a text id: the open text from memory, a part of a library work (`w:<id>:<n>`, from the library database) or an imported text. `glossMeta` takes `GL_CTX` = 5 words on each side; `glossStamp` is called by the reader when a gloss is made or changed; `glossMigrate` runs quietly 30 s after start-up (and before a glosses export) to fill in glosses that lack this data, text by text.

mem: the tokens of one text at a time
cpu: migration: tokenising each affected text, analyses for lemmata; one-time

components.name: Lemma names of default glosses
components.desc: Remembers the proper (accented) lemma for each default gloss, which is stored under an accent-free key.
components.detail: `lemmaNames` loads the map from the settings key `lgName` once; `lemmaNameSet` records a name when a default gloss is made; `lemmaNamesFill` fills in names for older default glosses from the lemmata of an opened text. The names are used in the glosses export.

components.name: Reattach review
components.desc: A dialog listing every found place with the old and new context, differences marked, to Accept or Reject; Auto-approve takes the certain ones.
components.detail: `glReview` shows for each gloss what was (words no longer present struck through) and what is now (new words marked; accent-only differences fainter), with Accept/Reject per gloss, Accept all, Reject all and Auto-approve. Accepted glosses get their new text id and word positions and fresh context (`glossMeta`) and are saved; the open text is reopened if it was affected.

components.name: When glosses are reattached
components.desc: Finds glosses that lost their text or no longer fit it, and starts the review after an import, after a backup restore, or by hand.
components.detail: `glOrphans` finds glosses of imported texts that were erased (and are not in the bin); `glMisfits` finds glosses whose stored word no longer matches the word at their place. `glAfterImport` offers orphans a place in a newly imported text; `glAfterRestore` re-places misfits after a backup is restored (called from the backup code in dialogs.js); `glFindPlace` lets the user pick any imported text or library work to search (Annotations → an erased text → Find a place).

mem: est. a few MB: tokens of all books of a chosen work
cpu: tokenising candidate texts; one-time per action

components.name: Highlighter & selection
components.desc: Marking passages in dictionary entries with a highlighter (mouse, Apple Pencil or long-press on Android), and the floating buttons that act on a selection.
components.detail: Highlights are saved per dictionary entry as character ranges of the entry's text (settings `hl|<dict>:<entry id>`), so they survive re-rendering and are included in backups. Selections work with the browser's selection on desktop and iPad, and with an app-drawn selection (CSS Custom Highlight API) on Android to avoid the system's selection menu.

store: small settings records per highlighted entry

components.name: Floating selection buttons
components.desc: The small button bar that appears at the bottom of the dictionary pane when text is selected (highlighter, + Gloss, + Default).
components.detail: `updateFab` shows or hides `#fabBar`, enables the highlighter only for a selection inside one entry, shows it as 'on' when the selection is already highlighted, and positions the bar over the pane. The + Gloss / + Default actions themselves are handled in the reader (they use `S.sel` / `S.lastSel`).

components.name: Selection to text offsets
components.desc: Converts between screen positions, DOM positions and character offsets inside an entry.
components.detail: `dictSelection` reports the current selection as `{eb, a, b, text}` when it lies inside one entry (else only its text), using either the app-drawn selection or the browser's. `offsetIn` and `posAt` convert DOM positions to character offsets and back; `caretAt` finds the text position under a point (caretRangeFromPoint / caretPositionFromPoint).

components.name: Painting highlights
components.desc: Draws the saved highlights into the entries on screen.
components.detail: `applyHighlights` repaints every entry of the page; `paintEntry` removes old marks (`unwrapMarks`), loads the ranges (also caching them in `S.hlCache` for the buttons) and `wrapRange` splits text nodes and wraps the parts in `<mark class=hl>`. `inlineGap` lets spaces between inline words be marked too, so a highlight has no gaps, while whitespace between blocks stays unmarked. `textNodes` is the shared text-node walker.

cpu: a text-node walk per entry; getComputedStyle for gap spaces

components.name: Apple Pencil selection
components.desc: On an iPad, dragging the Pencil over entry text selects it instead of scrolling; a Pencil tap works like a finger tap.
components.detail: `wirePencilSelect` intercepts stylus touches inside entries (non-passive touch listeners), tracks pointer events of type 'pen' and sets the browser selection from the start caret to the current caret once the pen has moved more than 4 px. Fingers keep scrolling and selecting as usual.

components.name: Highlight ranges
components.desc: Adds or removes highlighting for the selected text and saves it.
components.detail: `toggleHighlight` reads the entry's ranges, removes the selection from them if it is already fully covered (`subtractRange`), otherwise adds and merges it (`mergeRanges`), saves them and repaints the entry, then restores the same selection so it can still be glossed.

components.name: Android long-press selection
components.desc: On Android, a long press selects a word without the system menu, and dragging extends it word by word; a tap elsewhere ends it.
components.detail: `wireTouchSelect` starts a 450 ms timer on touch; when it fires it selects the word under the finger (`wordBounds` with the word-character class `WCH`) and vibrates briefly. Dragging then extends the range by whole words and blocks scrolling; the click that follows the long press is swallowed. The selection is stored in `S.tsel` (`setTsel`, `clearTsel`) and drawn with the CSS Custom Highlight API (`paintTsel`, `tselRange`); the context menu is suppressed in the text and dictionary panes.

gpu: the browser paints the custom highlight

components.name: Index of all texts
components.desc: An on-device index from lemma to every position in every text on the device, used by 'In all texts' and to speed up 'In this text' and the Library's word search.
components.detail: Stored in IndexedDB 'pult-search' (stores `lem`: lemma key → {part: positions}, and `part`: one record per indexed part plus `#meta`). Built in the background the first time it is needed; parts added later are indexed on the next search; a change of morphology data or of a text marks it out of date. Settings → Search can rebuild it.

mem: est. 20-100 MB while building (memo of analysed forms, up to 150k pending positions)
store: est. tens of MB for a large library (comma-separated positions per lemma and part)
cpu: building: a morphological analysis of every distinct form of every text, on the main thread in chunks

components.name: Building the index
components.desc: Indexes every part of every work and every imported text, a part at a time, showing progress.
components.detail: `allParts` lists the books of the library's works (`w:<id>:<n>`, versioned by the work) and imported texts (`i:<id>`, versioned by a quick hash `strHash`). `idxBuild` (single-flight via `S.idxBuilding`) tokenises each missing part (`partTokens`, applying stored annotations), maps each word to lemma keys (the annotated lemma or a memoised analysis), writes the part record, and flushes positions to `lem` in transactions of 400 keys once 150,000 words have accumulated; it yields after each part. `idxSig` records the morphology versions so the index can be marked stale.

mem: est. 20-100 MB: memo of every distinct form, pending positions
cpu: est. minutes for a large library; main thread, yielding per part

components.name: Index database
components.desc: Opens the 'pult-search' database.
components.detail: `searchDB` opens (and on first use creates) the database with stores `lem` and `part` and keeps the connection in `sdb`. Housekeeping in dialogs.js also uses it.

components.name: Querying the index
components.desc: Answers which parts contain a lemma and where, and how complete the index is.
components.detail: `idxLookup` reads the records of several lemma keys and returns sorted positions per part; `idxPositions` does it for one part (null when the part is not indexed). `idxState` compares indexed parts with the parts on the device (missing, stale, word count, build date); `partTitles` gives display names.

cpu: a few IndexedDB reads; idxState reads all part records and lists all works

components.name: Lemmata list
components.desc: The Lemmata tab: every lemma of the open section with its forms and frequency, and an editable default gloss for each; plus a vocabulary export.
components.detail: Built from the tokens of the open text section in memory, so it is instant and offline. Default glosses edited here are the same per-lemma glosses used across all texts.

mem: est. <1 MB: one row per lemma of the section
cpu: on opening the tab or changing sort/filter

components.name: Editing default glosses
components.desc: Saves a default gloss typed into the list and updates the text.
components.detail: `saveListGloss` cleans the text, remembers the lemma's name (`lemmaNameSet`), saves it through the reader's `setDefaultGloss` (settings `lg|<key>`), updates the counter and redraws the text so the gloss appears under the words.

cpu: a text redraw after each change

components.name: Vocabulary export
components.desc: Exports the list as a printable PDF list, a CSV spreadsheet, or an Anki import file.
components.detail: `vocabExportDialog` offers format and options (only lemmata with a gloss; forms and counts), then builds a table printed through `printHTML`, or a CSV (with BOM, quoted fields) or an Anki text file (tab-separated, HTML on, tagged with the text title) offered as a download link (the link is needed because iPad downloads must start from a tap). It respects the list's current filter and sort.

components.name: Lemmata tab
components.desc: Shows the list with counters, All / No gloss filter, sort buttons and a text field per lemma.
components.detail: `renderList` renders one row per lemma with its forms and count and a textarea holding the default gloss; empty ones stay one line high, filled ones are grown with `autoGrow`. It is redrawn when a text is opened.

mem: DOM of a few hundred to a few thousand rows

components.name: Vocabulary of the section
components.desc: Collects the lemmata of the open section with their forms, counts and first position.
components.detail: `vocabRows` groups the word tokens by lemma (or the word itself when not analysed), skipping all-capital speaker labels such as ΣΩ., and sorts by text order, A–Z (Greek collation) or frequency.

mem: a map over the section's tokens

components.name: Navigation & history
components.desc: Moving between entries: opening a word, Back/Forward through looked-up words, the full history list, and switching the pane between Entry, Lemmata and Map.
components.detail: Each look-up is a 'view' object; `showWord` starts a new history for a word tapped in the text and pushes onto the history for look-ups made inside the dictionary. A slim pill with ‹ and › sits on the line of the headword; holding it opens the whole history. The history lives only in memory (up to 200 steps).

mem: history of up to 200 small view objects
cpu: on taps only; layout measurement for the pill

components.name: Back and Forward pill
components.desc: The ‹ › pill at the top of the pane that steps back and forward through the looked-up words.
components.detail: `goBack` and `goFwd` move the current view between the `S.hist` and `S.fwd` stacks and redraw. `navButtons` shows the pill only on the Entry tab when there is somewhere to go, with tooltips from `viewName`. The wiring block (`wireDictNav`, top level) handles taps, long-press (500 ms) and right-click to open the history, Escape to close it, and stops touch scrolling of the history from scrolling the pane behind it.

components.name: History list
components.desc: A scrollable list of all words looked up in this session, opened by holding the pill; tapping one jumps there.
components.detail: `histList` lists history and forward steps newest first, marks the current one, shows each with its text reference or 'look-up', and sizes the list so it never runs past the pane's bottom edge (on phones the dictionary is the lower half). `goHist` rebuilds the back/forward stacks around the chosen position.

components.name: Pill alignment
components.desc: Keeps the navigation pill vertically centred on the first line of the headword so it takes no extra room.
components.detail: `alignNav` measures the headword and the pill and sets a top margin; it is re-run via a MutationObserver on the entry body and a ResizeObserver on the pane, coalesced into one animation frame.

cpu: a layout read after each redraw or resize

components.name: Open a word
components.desc: Opens the entry for a word, from the text, from inside an entry, or from search.
components.detail: `showWord` decides whether the word starts a new history (a word of the text) or is added to it (look-ups from the dictionary or search; the same word is not added twice), records the text reference with `refAt`, then switches to the Entry tab and calls `renderView`. When the Map tab is open the map stays in front and is told about the tapped word (`mapWordTapped`). `refAt` (the reference of a token, e.g. a line number) is also used by the reviews.

components.name: Pane tabs (Entry / Lemmata / Map)
components.desc: Switches the right-hand pane between the dictionary entry, the Lemmata list and the map.
components.detail: `showTab` toggles the three bodies and tab buttons and marks a short 'tab switch' period (`S.tabSw`, cleared by `releaseTabSw` or after 1.5 s) during which scroll events are not stored as reading positions. The map module also calls it.

components.name: Search engine
components.desc: The matching behind search: sorted headword lists of the installed dictionaries, Greek typed in Latin letters, wildcards, typo tolerance, and analysed forms.
components.detail: Each dictionary package carries its sorted lookup keys; they are merged per language into one packed string with an offset table for fast binary search. Queries are turned into one target per language and matched by prefix, wildcard or (when little is found) edit distance. Also used by the Library's search.

mem: est. 5-15 MB: packed Greek keys plus their folded twins, and Latin keys, kept for the session
store: a '#hw' record per dictionary database (est. 1-3 MB each)
cpu: building the lists once per session; per query binary search, sometimes a full fuzzy scan

components.name: Headword lists
components.desc: Loads and merges the headword keys of the searched dictionaries into compact sorted lists, one for Greek and one for Latin.
components.detail: `dictKeys` reads the key list stored with a dictionary (`#hw` in its database) or, for a dictionary installed before packages carried it, builds it once with a cursor over all records and stores it. `hwIndex` merges the dictionaries chosen by `scDicts` (switched on or all installed), packs them (`packKeys`: one string + Uint32Array offsets) and caches the result in `HW` keyed by a signature of dictionary versions; for Greek it also keeps a folded twin list (`foldG`: η→ε, ω→ο) pointing back to the real keys.

mem: est. 5-15 MB packed lists; est. 20-40 MB transient while splitting and sorting
cpu: once per session/language: split, de-duplicate and sort ~100-250k keys (est. 0.3-2 s); a full cursor pass for old dictionaries

components.name: Entries, snippets and forms
components.desc: Fetches what is shown for each hit: its headwords, dictionaries and the beginning of the first entry; and the analysed forms that match the query.
components.detail: `entriesIn` reads the key's bucket in each searched dictionary; `hitInfo` collects up to three headword spellings, the dictionary names and a `snippet` (entry text with the repeated headword stripped, cut at ~90 characters; parsed with a reusable `<template>` `snipEl`). `formsFor` looks the query up in the Greek morphology buckets (expanding e/o to all η/ω combinations, at most 64) or the Latin analysis, grouping readings by lemma (at most 60).

mem: buckets go through the analysis' shared cache (300 buckets)

components.name: Key matching
components.desc: Finds headword keys by prefix, by wildcard pattern, or by similarity when nothing matches exactly.
components.detail: `findKeys` returns exact matches first, then keys beginning with the query, shortest first (up to 600 candidates); with wildcards `wildHits` runs one multiline regex over the whole packed string. Only when there is no exact hit and fewer than 4 results does it fall back to `fuzzyHits`, which scans every key of similar length with `editDist` (Damerau-style, a swapped pair counts as one, with an early cut-off at 1 or 2 letters). `lowerBound`/`prefixHits` are the binary search.

cpu: prefix: microseconds; fuzzy/wildcard: a scan of all keys (est. 10-100 ms)

components.name: Query plan & transliteration
components.desc: Works out what to look for: Greek letters search Greek; Latin letters search Latin and, as transliterated Greek, Greek too.
components.detail: `searchPlan` normalises the query and builds targets per language, respecting the Greek/Latin button. `latinToGreek` transliterates (logos → λογος, psyche → ψυχη, with digraphs from `TRL`) or reads betacode when accent signs are present (`BETA`, lo/gos); ē/ō become η/ω. Wildcards `*` and `?` are kept through key folding (`keyKeepWild`, `hasWild`); `finalS` shows final sigma in displayed keys. These helpers are also used by the Library.

components.name: Search field & results
components.desc: The search field in the top bar: suggestions while typing, and a results page in the right pane with groups for dictionaries, forms, the open text and all texts.
components.detail: Typing shows up to 7/14/21 suggestions (headwords and analysed forms); Enter opens the results page as a 'search view' in the dictionary pane's history. Results groups are plug-ins (`SEARCH_GROUPS`) run in parallel, each filling its section when ready; their order and on/off are set in Settings → Search.

mem: est. a few MB of result DOM and the shared headword lists
cpu: per keystroke (debounced 110 ms) and per results page

components.name: In all texts (expanding a text)
components.desc: In the 'In all texts' group, tapping a text unfolds its occurrences with context; tapping one opens the text at that word.
components.detail: `togglePart` recomputes the lemma keys of the query, gets the positions in that part from the index (`idxLookup`), tokenises the part and lists each occurrence with its reference. `openHit` opens the text and selects the word. (The group itself, which lists texts by number of hits, is part of the results page.)

components.name: Search field
components.desc: Wires the search field: typing, arrow keys, Enter, Escape, and the optional Greek/Latin language button.
components.detail: `wireSearch` debounces input (110 ms) into suggestions, moves through them with the arrow keys, opens a suggestion or the results page on Enter, and handles taps on the results page (more …, headwords, forms, occurrences, parts of the index). `srchLangBtn` adds a button cycling Greek+Latin → Greek → Latin, drawn from the outline icon `SRCH_LANG_ICON` (the letters a and α of Gentium Book Plus).

components.name: In this text
components.desc: Lists every occurrence in the open work (all its parts) of the lemmata the query stands for, with reference and context; tapping one jumps there.
components.detail: `findLemmasInWork` walks the parts of the open work, using the index of all texts for a part when it covers it (`idxPositions`), otherwise the token's annotated lemma or a memoised morphological analysis per form; it stops at 2000 hits. `goToHit` opens the right part and `selectWordAt` marks and scrolls to the word and shows its entry.

mem: tokens of each part in turn; memo of analysed forms (S.lemMemo, kept for the session)
cpu: without the index: an analysis per distinct form of the whole work (est. up to seconds for large works)

components.name: Results page
components.desc: The full results page with sections Dictionaries, Forms, In this text and In all texts; long sections show the first rows and 'more …'.
components.detail: `openSearch` starts a new history with a search view; `renderSearch` draws the query (and its Greek transliteration), placeholders for the enabled groups, starts the shared lookups (keys, forms, lemmata) once and lets each group fill or remove its section; a counter drops stale pages. The four groups are registered at top level (`SEARCH_GROUPS.push`): Dictionaries (up to 40 headwords with dictionaries and snippet), Forms, In this text, In all texts. `moreList` (`SG_SHOW` = 6) and `sgSection` build the sections; `saveSearchQuery` is an empty hook for a future history.

cpu: per search: up to 40 snippet lookups plus the groups below

components.name: Suggestions while typing
components.desc: A drop-down list beneath the field with matching headwords (with a snippet of the first entry) and analysed forms.
components.detail: `updateSuggestions` builds a plan, finds keys (`findKeys`), adds up to two analysed forms when there is no exact headword, and fetches snippets (`hitInfo`); a sequence number (`sgSeq`) drops results of outdated keystrokes. `sugBox` creates the list (it keeps the keyboard open), `placeSug` fits it below the field and above the on-screen keyboard, `moveSuggestion`/`pickSuggestion` handle keyboard selection and opening, `hideSug` closes it, `langTag` marks Greek/Latin.

cpu: per keystroke after debounce: binary searches, possibly a fuzzy scan of all keys, a few bucket reads

components.name: Search settings
components.desc: The Search section of Settings: suggestions, transliteration, typo tolerance, order of result groups, which dictionaries are searched, and the index.
components.detail: Settings are kept in `S.sc` and saved as one record `searchCfg` (plus `srchLang` for the language button) in IndexedDB 'greekreader'.

components.name: Settings → Search panel
components.desc: Draws the Search section of the Settings dialog and reacts to its switches and buttons.
components.detail: `searchSettingsHTML` builds the sections from small helpers (`scSec`, `scLine`, `scSw` switches, `scSeg` segmented buttons) and `scGroupsHTML` (the result groups with drag grips; reordering is wired in dialogs.js). `wireSearchSettings` saves changes, clears the headword lists when the dictionary choice changes, and runs a full index rebuild with live progress (`scIdxInfo`, which shows texts indexed, word count, date, out of date).

cpu: progress refresh every 700 ms during a rebuild

components.name: Search preferences
components.desc: Loads and saves the search preferences with their defaults.
components.detail: `loadSearchCfg` merges the stored settings over `SC_DEF` (7 suggestions, transliteration on, lenient, typo distance 1, switched-on dictionaries …), validates the list length, and reconciles the saved group order with the registered `SEARCH_GROUPS`; `saveSearchCfg` writes it back.

components.name: Engines
components.desc: Libraries Pult builds on, and the browser features it relies on.

components.name: Browser platform
components.desc: The web platform features the app depends on: WebGL, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, the service worker, compression streams, Web Workers and canvas.
components.detail: Pult has no server-side logic: storage, offline use, decompression and all graphics run on these browser APIs. Missing features are reported rather than worked around (e.g. no DecompressionStream → a message asking to update iPadOS).

store: the quota of the site's origin (usage shown in Instruments)

components.name: Cache Storage
components.desc: Named HTTP response caches: the app files, map packages, saved relief, libraries and download parts.
components.detail: Used both by the service worker and directly from the page (`caches.open` in maps.js, maprelief.js, dialogs.js). Responses are stored under their real addresses, so cached map files and Mapterhorn tiles can be requested as ordinary URLs.

store: map packages and saved relief: up to GBs

components.name: Canvas 2D
components.desc: 2D drawing for the timeline, map overlays and exports, textures, glyphs and offline relief tiles.
components.detail: getContext('2d') appears in nine scripts (app, library, timeline, map layers, saved maps, sun/sky, relief, TinySDF); OffscreenCanvas and createImageBitmap decode Mapterhorn tiles in the service worker (`enlargeDem`) and in maplibre-contour.

mem: canvases while open (map exports can be large)

components.name: IndexedDB
components.desc: The browser database holding settings, texts, dictionaries, the library, places and the search index.
components.detail: Opened with `indexedDB.open` in core.js (settings and one database per dictionary), library.js, maps.js (places) and search.js. The app asks for persistent storage (`navigator.storage.persist`) at start and before downloads, and shows usage and free space from `navigator.storage.estimate`.

store: hundreds of MB with several dictionaries and texts

components.name: Compression streams
components.desc: Built-in gzip / deflate (de)compression used for packages, texts and documents.
components.detail: DecompressionStream('gzip') unpacks .gdpkg.gz dictionary packages and .json.gz works in `readPackage` (analysis.js); 'deflate-raw' reads .docx/.odt entries in `zipEntry` (dialogs.js); CompressionStream('deflate-raw') writes zipped exports (export.js). pmtiles.js also uses it for archive directories.

mem: a package is unpacked to one text string (tens of MB for LSJ) before parsing

components.name: Service worker
components.desc: The background script that makes the app work offline and answers requests from the caches.
components.detail: Registered in app.js (`navigator.serviceWorker.register('sw.js')`, not on file://); it imports reliefsw.js and routes requests by path and host. Activation deletes old app caches but keeps 'pult-maps', 'pult-relief' and 'pult-lib'.

mem: a separate small JS context (+ up to 48 enlarged relief tiles)
cpu: per request routing; tile enlarging offline

components.name: WebGL
components.desc: The GPU drawing API under the map: MapLibre's renderer and the three.js obelisk share one WebGL context.
components.detail: Custom layers ('skybodies' 2D, 'obel3d' 3D) draw into MapLibre's context. When the system takes the graphics memory back (common on phones), the 'webglcontextlost' event is turned into a readable error with a retry button.

mem: GPU buffers and textures mirrored in RAM (est.)

components.name: Web Workers
components.desc: Background threads for heavy map work, so the page stays responsive.
components.detail: MapLibre runs a worker pool (sized from hardwareConcurrency) for tile parsing; maplibre-contour runs its own worker; both are created from blob URLs. Pult's own scripts run on the main thread.

mem: one JS context per worker (est. 5-20 MB each)
cpu: tile parsing and contours off the main thread

components.name: maplibre-contour
components.desc: Library (Michael Barry, BSD-3) that turns elevation tiles into contour lines on the fly and serves elevation data to the app.
components.detail: Loaded as a classic script (`addScript('maplibre-contour.js')` in `reliefInit`) only when relief is available (online, or an area is saved). One `DemSource` for Mapterhorn is created per session with worker on, a cache of 24 tiles and a 30 s timeout.
components.netNote: works offline from saved relief areas

mem: est. ~25-40 MB: up to 24 decoded 512 px DEM tiles + contour tiles
cpu: in a worker: WebP decode + isoline tracing per tile

components.name: DEM source
components.desc: The library entry point: `mlcontour.DemSource`, which fetches and decodes elevation tiles and plugs itself into MapLibre.
components.detail: The whole bundled library (one minified UMD script defining the global `mlcontour`, with its worker code embedded as a blob) is this declaration. `setupMaplibre` registers its protocols; `getDemTile` returns decoded heights, which Pult uses for heights on tap and profiles of drawn lines (`profileOf`).
components.netNote: tiles from Mapterhorn or the saved-relief cache

cpu: request bookkeeping on the main thread

components.name: Contour vector tiles
components.desc: Contour lines delivered to MapLibre as vector tiles through `contourProtocolUrl`.
components.detail: maprelief.js builds the source 'contours' (layer 'contours', keys 'ele' and 'level', overzoom 1, multiplier for feet or metres); the numbers are labelled with the self-made glyphs from TinySDF.

components.name: Contour worker
components.desc: A Web Worker that decodes the WebP tiles and traces the contour lines away from the page.
components.detail: Started from a blob URL built from the bundled worker code; decodes with createImageBitmap and OffscreenCanvas, then runs marching-squares isolines at the levels Pult asks for (spacing from `contSpacing`, units from the settings).

mem: decoded tiles in the worker (est. 1 MB per 512 px tile)

components.name: MapLibre GL JS
components.desc: The open-source WebGL map renderer that draws the whole map: vector and raster layers, globe, 3D terrain, hillshade, labels.
components.detail: Downloaded with the Base map package (not part of the app files) and loaded on demand by `loadMapLib` (maps.js) from the cache 'pult-maps'. Version 5.24.0 (base/lib5) is used; 4.7.1 (base/lib) only if an older download lacks version 5. Pult hooks into it through custom protocols (pmtiles://, pultglyph://, maplibre-contour's), custom layers (sky bodies, three.js obelisk) and two small source patches.
components.netNote: needs the Base map package (downloaded once)

mem: est. 30-150 MB: parsed engine, tile caches, GeoJSON sources, style
cpu: tile parsing in its worker pool; style rebuilds on setting changes; per-frame layout
gpu: every map frame: all layers, globe, terrain

components.name: Pult's patches to MapLibre
components.desc: Small text replacements in the MapLibre 5 script so hillshading follows the real sun at every point, and the obelisk is lit by its own sun.
components.detail: `shadePatchedLib` (maprelief.js) fetches the script text, applies `SHADE_PATCH` (new uniforms u_lngrange, u_sun, u_sun2 and per-pixel sun azimuth and night fade in the hillshade shader, fed from self.__pultSun) and `OB_PATCH` (fill-extrusion light from self.__pultObLight), and loads the result from a blob URL. `enginePatch` applies each group whole or not at all: if a piece is not found exactly (another version), that group is skipped and the engine runs unchanged.

mem: a second copy of the ~1 MB script as a string and blob while loading
store: nothing stored (patched in memory at each start)
cpu: once per map start: string splits over 1 MB
gpu: a few extra shader instructions per hillshade pixel

components.name: Custom tile protocols
components.desc: Address schemes MapLibre calls back into for data: pmtiles:// (map packages), pultglyph:// (contour figures) and maplibre-contour's DEM and contour schemes.
components.detail: Registered with `maplibregl.addProtocol`: `pmInit` (maps.js) for PMTiles, `glyphInit` (maprelief.js) for the self-made glyphs, and `DemSource.setupMaplibre` for elevation and contour tiles. They let fully offline data and in-app generated data appear to the engine as ordinary tile URLs.

components.name: MapLibre 4.7 (fallback)
components.desc: The previous engine version, used only when a Base map downloaded before v295 lacks version 5.
components.detail: `engineDir` checks the cache for base/lib5/maplibre-gl.js and otherwise loads base/lib unpatched. Features that need version 5 (height colours, the sun-shading patch) are then missing; `engineMajor` lets the relief code tell.
components.netNote: from the Base map package

components.name: MapLibre 5.24
components.desc: The map engine in use: globe projection, 3D terrain, hillshade, color-relief, fill-extrusion and custom WebGL layers.
components.detail: Loaded from maps/base/lib5 (script + CSS) via a patched blob URL (see the patches). The map is created in `showMap1` with globe or Mercator projection, max pitch 85, zoom 0-16; a 'webglcontextlost' listener reports lost graphics memory on phones. Version 5 is required for color-relief (height colours) and the globe atmosphere.
components.netNote: from the Base map package

mem: est. 30-150 MB with tile caches and GeoJSON sources
cpu: worker-pool tile parsing; main-thread layout and placement per frame
gpu: renders every frame while the map moves; terrain and globe add cost

components.name: pmtiles.js
components.desc: Library (Protomaps, 4.4.1) that reads tiles out of single-file PMTiles archives.
components.detail: Shipped in the Base map package (base/lib/pmtiles.js) and loaded after MapLibre when present; `pmInit` registers its `Protocol` as pmtiles://. Instead of HTTP range requests, Pult gives it a `CacheSource` that slices the whole archive blob kept in the cache 'pult-maps', so every PMTiles package works offline.
components.netNote: archives come from downloaded map packages

mem: archive directories + the blob handle per package (est. a few MB)
cpu: directory decompression and lookups per tile

components.name: pmtiles:// protocol
components.desc: Answers MapLibre's tile requests for pmtiles:// sources.
components.detail: `pmUrl` (maps.js) adds one `PMTiles` instance per downloaded archive and returns its pmtiles:// address for the style; the protocol finds the archive and returns the tile bytes.

components.name: Archive reader
components.desc: Reads the archive header and directories and locates each tile's byte range.
components.detail: Reads through `CacheSource.getBytes` (blob.slice of the cached file); directories are gzip-compressed and unpacked with DecompressionStream.

components.name: three.js
components.desc: The 3D library (r169) used to draw the porphyry obelisk as a lit, textured model inside the map.
components.detail: Imported lazily as an ES module (`threeLib` in mapsun.js) only when the obelisk is shown; if it cannot load, MapLibre's fill-extrusion blocks stand in. The service worker keeps lib/ in the cache 'pult-lib' across app updates.
components.netNote: fetched once from the app's site, then from the cache 'pult-lib'

mem: est. 3-8 MB: parsed module + one scene
cpu: parse once; scene update per frame while shown
gpu: one small mesh per map frame

components.name: Module loading
components.desc: Loads lib/three-0.169.0.module.min.js by dynamic import, once.
components.detail: `threeLib` memoises the import promise; failures are logged and return null so the map keeps the extrusion fallback. The service worker's lib/ rule serves the file cache-first from 'pult-lib' (the version is in the file name, so no revalidation is needed).
components.netNote: first use needs the network

components.name: Renderer in the map's GL context
components.desc: A three.js WebGLRenderer drawing into MapLibre's own canvas and WebGL context as a custom 3D layer.
components.detail: `obel3dLayer` (mapsun.js) creates the renderer with MapLibre's gl context (autoClear off), a camera fed from the map's projection matrix, MeshStandardMaterial with a 256 px procedural porphyry texture, and sun and sky lights. The depth buffer is shared, so hills and the globe hide the model.

gpu: a few hundred triangles with PBR shading per frame

components.name: TinySDF
components.desc: Mapbox's small library (2.3.0, BSD-2) that draws letters as signed distance fields in a canvas; Pult uses it for the figures of contour numbers.
components.detail: Imported as a module by `pultGlyphs` (maprelief.js), it renders 15 characters (digits, comma, minus, point, space) in Source Sans 3 600 at 24 px, which Pult packs into a glyph protocol buffer for MapLibre. This avoids a glyph server and keeps contour labels offline in the app's own font.

components.name: Glyph drawing
components.desc: Draws one character into a canvas and converts its alpha into a distance field.
components.detail: The `TinySDF` class (module top level) uses one 2D canvas of font size + 4 × buffer (36 px here), draws the glyph, and maps alpha through the gamma-corrected `alphaTable` into inner and outer distance grids before running the transform.

components.name: Distance transform
components.desc: The Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher Euclidean distance transform behind the distance fields.
components.detail: `edt` runs `edt1d` over columns and then rows of the glyph area; `INF` (1e20) marks unset cells.

cpu: linear in pixels, once per glyph

components.name: Export
components.desc: Exports and backups of what you made.

components.name: Export dialog
components.desc: Exports the open text as it is shown (PDF via printing, HTML or Word), the whole text, a range from/to, or a passage marked by tapping.
components.detail: `exportDialog` remembers the last choices (format, range, glosses, grammar line, colours) and builds the right output; HTML and Word files are offered as a tap-to-save link with their size (needed on the iPad), revoked after 60 s.

components.name: Export options
components.desc: The dialog itself: format, range (whole text, from-to, selection) and what to include.
components.detail: `exportDialog` lists the reference points for from/to selects, shows the marked passage, starts marking when 'Mark in the text' is pressed, computes the range and label, calls `exportModel`, and dispatches to printing, `exportHTMLFile` or `exportDocx`. On first use, glosses, grammar and colours default to what is currently shown; later the last choices are kept for the session.

components.name: Export title
components.desc: The title used in exports: author – work – book (or the imported text's title), plus the exported range.
components.detail: `exportTitle` is shared by the text export and the vocabulary export, and is also used for file names (with characters not allowed in file names removed).

components.name: Word (.docx)
components.desc: Exports the text as a Word document; with glosses or a grammar line it becomes interlinear, each printed line a borderless table with one column per word.
components.detail: The .docx is written by hand: WordprocessingML text, three package files and a minimal ZIP writer, without any library. The same XML and ZIP helpers are reused by the glosses export and the Library.

mem: est. a few MB: the XML and the measuring DOM
cpu: interlinear: lays out the whole text off-screen and measures every word

components.name: Document body & interlinear layout
components.desc: Writes the text as Word paragraphs, or as interlinear line tables when glosses or grammar are included.
components.detail: `exportDocxBody` writes running text as one paragraph per block with references as small grey numbers. For interlinear output it renders the export HTML off-screen at A4 text width (643 px), reads which words share a line from their positions (`getBoundingClientRect`), and writes each line as a fixed-layout table (reference column + one column per word, widths in twips) with the word, its grammar and its gloss lines stacked, separated by tiny paragraphs so Word does not merge the tables. Note: it re-queries the block's words for each word (`querySelectorAll('.w')[k++]`), so very long blocks cost quadratic time.

mem: off-screen copy of the text DOM plus the XML string
cpu: layout + one rect per word; est. seconds for a long book

components.name: Word package
components.desc: Wraps the document body into the files a .docx needs.
components.detail: `exportDocx` adds the A4 page setup (2 cm margins) and the `[Content_Types].xml` and `_rels/.rels` parts, and zips them with `zipFiles`.

components.name: WordprocessingML helpers
components.desc: Small builders for Word text runs and paragraphs.
components.detail: `wRun` writes a run with font, size, bold/italic and colour; `wP` a paragraph with spacing and alignment; `xe` escapes XML. Also used by the glosses export, the Library's search export and (`xe`) by mapsun.js.

components.name: ZIP writer
components.desc: A minimal ZIP writer, enough for .docx files.
components.detail: `zipFiles` compresses each file with the browser's `CompressionStream('deflate-raw')` where available, otherwise stores it; `zipStore` writes local headers, the central directory and the end record with a CRC-32 (table cached on the function), UTF-8 names, and returns a Blob typed as .docx. Also used by the glosses export and the Library.

cpu: CRC and compression, once per export

components.name: HTML & PDF
components.desc: Exports as an HTML file with the fonts embedded, or as PDF through the browser's print dialog.
components.detail: Both use the same markup (`exportHTML` + `EXPORT_CSS`): each word stacked over its grammar line and glosses, references in a left margin. PDF uses the browser's own printing ('Save as PDF'; iPad: share → Save to Files).

mem: HTML file string incl. ~0.8 MB of base64 fonts
cpu: once per export; printing lays out the whole text

components.name: HTML file with embedded fonts
components.desc: A standalone .html file that looks the same on any computer because the fonts are inside it.
components.detail: `exportHTMLFile` wraps the markup in a page with print rules (A4, 2 cm margins). `fontFacesInline` fetches fonts.css and every woff2 it references and inlines them as base64 data URLs; if any fetch fails it returns no fonts at all (the file then uses the system's fonts). The fonts come from the app cache when offline. (The inventory's 'top level' entry of export.js is text inside this template.) It is also used by the glosses export and the Library.
components.netNote: fonts are fetched from the app's offline cache when there is no network

mem: ~0.6 MB of fonts held as ~0.8 MB base64 text plus copies while splicing

components.name: Printing (PDF)
components.desc: Prints any export through the browser's print dialog, from which it can be saved as PDF.
components.detail: `printHTML` puts the HTML and its CSS into a hidden `#printRoot`, sets the `printing` class (style.css then hides the app while printing), calls `window.print()` and cleans up after `afterprint` (or after 1.5 s where that event is missing). `exportPrint` is the text export's use; the vocabulary list, glosses export and Library use it too.

mem: the print DOM of the whole text
cpu: the browser lays out and paginates the document

components.name: Export markup
components.desc: Turns the text model into HTML: words with optional colours, grammar and glosses below them, references in the margin.
components.detail: `exportHTML` writes each block (heading, section title, verse line, paragraph) and each word as an inline-flex column; `EXPORT_CSS` styles it for A4 with Gentium Book Plus and Source Sans 3. The same markup is also measured to lay out the Word export.

components.name: Text model for export
components.desc: Reads the text as displayed into plain data: blocks of words, punctuation, line breaks and references, with each word's colour, grammar line and glosses.
components.detail: `exportModel` walks the reader's DOM (`textRoot`), taking word-class colours from the current colour settings (only switched-on classes), the grammar line (`.gm`) and glosses (default glosses flagged). With a range it keeps the words a…b plus the references and punctuation around them, so a passage starts and ends cleanly. Because it reads the DOM, the export is exactly what is shown (e.g. vowel lengths if shown).

mem: est. a few MB for a long book
cpu: one DOM walk of the whole text

components.name: Choosing a passage
components.desc: Lets the reader export only part of a text: between two reference points (lines, sections or paragraphs) or a passage marked by tapping its first and last word.
components.detail: Reference points are taken from the text's tokens; when a text has none, its paragraphs are numbered.

components.name: Marking a passage in the text
components.desc: After 'Mark in the text …', the first tap marks the first word and the second the last; a bar at the bottom shows the count and an Export button.
components.detail: `exportPickStart` enters the picking mode (`S.exPick`, body class `expick`); `exportPickPaint` colours the marked words and draws the floating bar `#exBar` over the text pane. The taps themselves are handled in app.js.

cpu: class toggles over the marked words

components.name: Reference points
components.desc: Lists the lines (verse), sections (prose) or paragraphs of the current book for the From/To choice.
components.detail: `exportRefs` collects reference tokens followed by a word, decides verse or prose (the work's flag, or whether most references are line numbers), falls back to '¶ n' paragraphs, and gives each point its end and a short label (first four words). `exportSelLabel` describes a marked passage as 'first words … last words'.

components.name: Library
components.desc: The catalogue of texts: finding, downloading and arranging them, with their timeline.

components.name: Library overview
components.desc: The Library's main page: tabs (Bibliotheca, Armarium, Scriptorium, Favourites), search, filters, sorting and the list of authors and works.
components.detail: All state lives in one view object (`libView`, saved as setting 'libView'). The list is rebuilt as HTML on each change; authors are folded <details> whose works are only drawn when opened, and flat lists show 250 rows at a time. A search also looks for the word in the texts on the device.

components.name: Filter panel
components.desc: The panel opened by the sieve button: language, prose or verse, undated works, and periods on the date line; active filters show as removable chips when it is closed.
components.detail: `libControlsHTML` builds the panel with joined switches (`seg`) and the date line; `libActiveHTML` the chips. The sieve icon (`sieveIcon`) is drawn as SVG with a finer mesh the more the list is narrowed: `sieveStep` counts works in the tab and those shown and adds a line pair each time the list halves (up to 7). `filterIcon`/`renderLibControls` refresh button, chips and panel. `chip` (toggle chips) is no longer used by the current panel.

cpu: `sieveStep` re-checks all works on each render

components.name: Authors and works list
components.desc: Draws the tabs and the list: authors with their works, or flat lists of works, with counts, markers and a footer of what is on the device.
components.detail: `lmOverviewHTML` lays out the page; `renderLibList` fills the list for the tab and sort: authors as folded <details> (unfolded when the search hits a title, or on short personal shelves), flat lists capped at 250 rows with 'Show more' (+500), Favourites flat, Scriptorium via its own module, and Armarium with a 'Recently removed' group (`trashGroupHTML`). `lmAuthorHTML` and `lmRowHTML` draw an author and a work row (marker ribbon `RIBBON`, Greek title, language, form, parts, words). `lmTabsHTML` shows counts per tab and the Import button; `libFootHTML` sums sizes with `mb`. `FLAME` (a favourite flame icon) is unused now.

mem: list HTML: ≤ 485 author rows or ≤ 250+ work rows, est. 1-5 MB DOM
cpu: rebuilds innerHTML of the list on each change

components.name: Search and matching
components.desc: Decides which works pass the current tab, filters and search text; the search matches authors and titles in English, Latin or Greek.
components.detail: `workPasses` checks tab, language, prose/verse, the author's year against the chosen periods (a single year counts ±25) and the folded search text against author, title, Greek title and id; `fold` drops accents and final sigma. `libQGreek` converts Latin letters to Greek (logos → λογος) using search.js, and `libQGNote` shows that conversion under the field. `libAuthors` merges the catalogue (or, without one, the installed works) with imported texts; `libFilter` gives an author's matching works in order. `authorOf` and `workLang` supply the author and language. `libSources` (list of sources) is no longer used.

cpu: one pass over ~2,500 works per change (debounced 150 ms while typing)

components.name: Sorting
components.desc: Sorts by author or by title, each alphabetically (Α–Ω) or chronologically (BC–AD), with a remembered direction for each kind.
components.detail: `SORTS` lists the four combinations; `sortBarHTML` draws two button pairs whose order icons are Gentium capitals stored as SVG outlines (`SORT_ICON`, `sortIcon`), and tapping the lit one reverses it. `sortedWorks` makes the flat lists (by title, and Favourites), putting undated works at the end of chronological order.

cpu: sort of up to ~2,500 works per change

components.name: View settings
components.desc: Remembers the open tab, filters, sort order and date-line settings of the Library between sessions.
components.detail: `libView` fills in defaults and migrates settings of older versions (favourites/mine as filters, old sort names, a single default period, the old century slider) into the current shape; `saveLibView` stores it. `filtersOn` and `filtersAtDefault` tell whether any filter is set and whether reset would change anything; `ftDef` gives the default periods. `LTABS` names the four tabs.

components.name: Words in the texts on this device
components.desc: While searching the Library, also lists the downloaded works that contain the typed word (any of its forms), with the number of places; a tap opens a lemma search in that work.
components.detail: `lmWords` runs when the search has 2+ letters, the word index is built and Settings → Search allows it: it finds the headword(s) with search.js (`searchPlan`, `findKeys`, `formsFor`), looks them up in the word index (`idxLookup`) and counts places per work. A sequence number drops answers to older keystrokes.

components.name: Catalogue and downloads
components.desc: The list of all works available on the website (Perseus, First1KGreek, CSEL: 485 authors, 2,547 works) and the downloading of works, singly or by author.
components.detail: The catalogue (texts/catalog.json, ~1.1 MB) is fetched without cache when online and saved in settings, so the Library also opens offline with the last known copy. Downloads go through the shared download queue of dialogs.js; this part does the fetching with progress and the per-work and per-author download buttons.

mem: the parsed catalogue, est. 5-10 MB of objects

components.netNote: catalogue and downloads need the network; the saved catalogue and installed works work offline

components.name: Download by author
components.desc: One button per author that downloads all their (filtered) works at once, shows how much is already on the device, and offers 'Download the rest' and 'Remove all'.
components.detail: `authState` sums sizes of the author's works that pass the filters (on device, missing, downloading, failed, in the bin); `authIconHTML` draws the button filled in proportion, with retry (↻), restore or stop states. `authQueue` asks for persistent storage and queues all missing works in the shared download queue; `authPaint` updates the author's button at most once per animation frame as downloads progress. The script's top-level click handlers run these buttons and the pop-up choices (stop, restore all, erase all, remove all), the 'Erase all' of Recently removed, and the back gesture / Esc that steps from a page to the overview.

cpu: recount on each progress tick, throttled to one per frame

components.netNote: downloading needs the network; restore/remove work offline

components.name: Download a work
components.desc: Fetches one work's package from the website with a progress fill, then installs it.
components.detail: `downloadWork` is called by the download queue (`runDownloads` in dialogs.js) for ids 'work:<id>'. It streams texts/works/<id>.json.gz (median ~27 kB, largest ~2.8 MB) and reports progress up to 90% against the size in the catalogue, then installs it with `installWork`, updates the list of installed works, reopens the text if it is the one being read and redraws the Library.

mem: the downloaded chunks until installed (≤ ~2.8 MB compressed)
store: code; the result goes to greekreader-lib
cpu: streaming; installing is counted under Install

components.netNote: needs the network; a work in the 7-day bin is restored offline instead

components.name: Catalogue loading
components.desc: Gets the catalogue of available works, from the network when possible, otherwise the copy saved on the device.
components.detail: `fetchCatalog` requests texts/catalog.json with 'no-cache' through `fetchT` (gives up after 6 s, because offline iOS requests often hang); on success it saves the catalogue and its date in settings ('catalog', 'catalogAt'), otherwise it falls back to the saved one and marks the session offline (`S.catOnline`). `cachedCatalog` returns the saved copy at once so the Library opens without waiting; `netCheck` (dialogs.js) re-fetches when the copy is older than a day. `indexCatalog` builds lookups by work id and author.

mem: parsed catalogue + two index maps, est. 5-10 MB
store: settings 'catalog' (~1.1 MB structured copy) in greekreader
cpu: JSON parse of ~1.1 MB once per session

components.netNote: fresh copy online; saved copy offline

components.name: Download button of a work
components.desc: The round button beside each work: download, downloading, on this device, revision available, or restore from the bin.
components.detail: `lmIcon` asks dialogs.js (`dlIcon`) for the button with the work's state: installed, a revision available (when notices are on), size, disabled while offline, or a restore arrow for a work in the 7-day bin. Imported texts get a button only while in the bin. `DLICON` is an older download-arrow SVG that the current code no longer uses.
components.netNote: downloading needs the network; restore and delete work offline

components.name: Library menu
components.desc: The full-screen Library dialog with two levels: the overview and the page of a work; the title button opens the open work's page, ☰ → Library the overview.
components.detail: Opening the menu loads everything the lists need (settings, catalogue, installed works, imported texts, traces, bin, revisions) and checks the network. The menu redraws itself in place after each choice or download and handles the back gesture (page → overview → closed).

mem: est. 1-5 MB of state and HTML
cpu: preparation on open (reads all glosses and some settings keys)

components.name: Work keys and info
components.desc: Names every work by one key (a library id, or 'imp:<n>' for an imported text) and finds its details on the device or in the catalogue.
components.detail: `curKey` is the key of the open text, `textIdOf` turns a key and part into a reader text id, `keyOfText` does the reverse (also used by glosses and dialogs). `workInfo` merges catalogue and installed record (installed flag, parts). `lmOffline` reports whether the catalogue could not be reached this session.

components.name: Opening and moving in the menu
components.desc: Opens the Library at the overview or at a work's page, moves between them and redraws after changes.
components.detail: `libraryDialog` and `navDialog` call `libMenu`, which runs `libPrep` (settings 'libView', 'opened', 'favs', 'recent', 'revRej', 'revOn'; catalogue; installed works; imported texts; traces; previous versions; flagged glosses; bin; `netCheck`) and opens the shared dialog, pushing a history entry for the back gesture. `lmGo` switches page keeping the overview's scroll position; `lmRender` redraws the current page in place.

cpu: `libPrep` reads several stores on each open

components.netNote: works offline; a reachability check refreshes the catalogue when online

components.name: Your traces in works
components.desc: Finds where you left glosses, markers or chosen word analyses, to list annotated works and to mark outline rows with a bookmark or pen sign.
components.detail: `lmTraces` counts glosses per work (reads all of 'glosses') and collects works with markers ('mk|' keys) or chosen analyses ('an|' keys). `partTraces` reads one part's gloss positions and marker (cached per menu opening); `rangeHas` checks by binary search whether a range of words holds any, `nodeRange`/`refSpan` give an outline node's word range, and `marksHTML` draws the signs (`BMARK`, `GMARK`).

mem: all glosses read once per opening (est. < 1-5 MB)
cpu: one scan of all glosses per menu opening

components.name: Menu taps and keys
components.desc: Handles everything tapped or typed in the Library menu: tabs, search field, filters, sorting, favourites, Scriptorium edits, outline, find and export buttons.
components.detail: `wireLibrary` installs document-level listeners once: search input (debounced 150 ms), folding authors (works drawn on unfold), Enter in the find field, long-press on a tab to show its hint, and one big click handler dispatching on data attributes (view switch with per-tab scroll position, filter/sort changes, favourites, delete/edit of imported texts, outline folding, jumping to sections, find results, export). `onText` makes a row open only when the tap is on its text, not the empty part. It also starts the date line's gestures.

components.name: Moving through a text
components.desc: Everything about where you are in a text: the title bar with work, book and section, references, Go to, next/previous book, saving the reading position and the full-screen reading mode.
components.detail: Although it lives in library.js, this part serves the reader. References are worked out from the text's tokens; the current section follows the word at the top of the text pane.

components.name: Go to a place
components.desc: Jumps to a place typed or chosen ('245c', '1.6', '14.1.6', line 120), to the next/previous book, or to a word, briefly flashing it.
components.detail: `goTo` matches the typed reference in the open part, else as 'part.reference' in another part (line numbers to the section beginning there); `goPlace` opens a part and scrolls to a reference or word; `scrollToWord` scrolls the pane so the word sits near the top and flashes it for 1.4 s, then saves the position. `stepBook` moves to the next or previous book. Map cards, saved maps, search and drawings use these too.

components.name: Reading mode
components.desc: Full-screen mode with only the text; leave with Esc or by swiping in from the middle of the right edge.
components.detail: `setReading` toggles the 'reading' class, requests or exits full screen, shows a hint and resizes glosses. `wireReading` wires the button, Esc, leaving full screen, and the edge swipe (pointer events within 40 px of the right edge in the middle third; past the screen's middle it closes), blocking browser scroll/back while pulling.

components.name: Reading position and recently read
components.desc: Remembers where you were in each text and keeps the 'Recently read' list with the section and a line of text.
components.detail: `saveReadPos` stores the scroll position ('pos|<text>') and, with the word-anchored layout, the top word and offset ('pw|<text>'), then calls `touchRecent`, which puts the work at the top of the recent list (one entry per work: part, section, first 12 words at the top, time; max 60) and saves it after 300 ms.

components.name: References and current section
components.desc: Finds the references (sections, lines, Stephanus pages, or numbered paragraphs when there are none) of a part and the section you are reading.
components.detail: `refsOf` reads reference tokens from the text (falling back to '¶ 1, ¶ 2' per paragraph), marks verse texts and gives each reference its first seven words. `topWord` binary-searches the drawn words for the first one at the top of the pane; `curRef` finds the last section starting at or before it. `partRefs` gets references of another part of the open work (cached). `refGroups` (an older chapter-list grouping) is unused.

cpu: binary searches on scroll; tokenising a part once

components.name: Title bar
components.desc: Shows 'Author › Work › Book › Section' (on narrow screens the work above and '14 › 3.2' below), updating the section while scrolling.
components.detail: `titleBar` builds the title when a text opens; `updateSecTitle` shows the current section and, when the map is open with a section or chapter scope, refreshes its data after 250 ms. `secRoom` measures the widest reference of the book on a canvas so the buttons beside the title do not move, and switches to short book names when the title would be cut; the script's top-level code re-runs it on window resize (debounced 200 ms). `stripCommon` turns 'Book 1, Book 2' into '1, 2'.

cpu: measuring once per book; a binary search per scroll update

components.name: Revisions of works
components.desc: When the catalogue has a corrected version of a downloaded work, the Library shows a faint 'rev.'; the work's page lists the changed passages, corrected annotations and structure changes, to accept or reject as a whole.
components.detail: Accepting moves glosses, chosen analyses, place marks, the marker and reading position to their words in the new text, flags glosses whose words changed, and keeps the previous version 7 days so you can return to it.

mem: both versions' tokens + diff traces, est. 10-50 MB for a large work
store: previous version kept in settings for 7 days
cpu: word-level diff on the main thread

components.netNote: fetching a revision needs the network; returning to the previous version works offline

components.name: Fetch and compare a revision
components.desc: Fetches the corrected version (without installing it) and compares it part by part, showing progress.
components.detail: `revCompare` downloads texts/works/<id>.json.gz, unpacks it, pairs parts by number (or by name when the counts differ), applies annotations to both versions, runs `revPart` on each pair yielding to the browser between parts, and notes added, removed or renamed parts and changed references. `revOpen` starts it once per work and redraws the page as it advances.

mem: new package + both versions' tokens (est. 10-50 MB for the largest works)
cpu: unpack + tokenise + diff of every part

components.netNote: needs the network to fetch the corrected version

components.name: Word-by-word comparison
components.desc: Compares two versions of a part word by word and punctuation mark, giving the changed passages and a map from old word numbers to new.
components.detail: `revSeq` turns tokens into a sequence of words and punctuation marks; `revMatch` is a Myers diff after trimming the common start and end, giving up (whole part 'rewritten') beyond 1,500 edits. `revPart` builds the old→new word map, the changed passages with five words of context and their reference, the words whose lemma/grammar annotation changed (first 40 kept as examples) and the old and new reference lists.

mem: diff trace grows with edits squared (≤ ~1,500 edits; est. up to ~10 MB per part)
cpu: O((N+M)·D) diff per part, main thread

components.name: Glosses to check
components.desc: Lists glosses whose words changed in a revision, with their place and words, to jump to and mark as checked.
components.detail: `revFlagsLoad` counts flagged glosses ('rv') per work from all glosses; `revFlagsHTML` lists them per part with reference, words and gloss text, with 'Checked' and 'All checked' buttons.

cpu: scan of all glosses when the menu opens

components.name: Moving your traces
components.desc: Carries your glosses, chosen analyses, place marks, marker and reading position over to the matching words in the other version.
components.detail: `revNear` finds the same word, or next to the nearest unchanged word. `revMoveTraces` rewrites each part's glosses (flagging with 'rv' those whose words changed), moves 'an|' and 'pl|' settings only where the word stayed the same, and moves the marker 'mk|', word position 'pw|' and scroll position 'pos|'.

components.name: Revision notice and page
components.desc: The 'rev.' marker, the notes on a work's page, and the page 'Library › Work › Revision' with the summary, changed passages and corrected annotations.
components.detail: `revAvail` checks that the installed version differs from the catalogue's and was not rejected. `revBackHTML` adds 'Return to the previous version' and the count of glosses to check; `revPageHTML` shows progress, the summary (passages, annotations, structure), Accept/Reject, up to 300 passages per part with deletions and insertions, and up to 40 annotation examples. `wireRevisions` handles these buttons and also the Settings → Library inputs (date-line range, era names, restore defaults, notices, reconsider rejected).
components.netNote: the notice uses the last catalogue

components.name: Accept, reject, return
components.desc: Accepts a revision (installing it), rejects it (the notice returns only for a newer one), or returns to the previous version within 7 days.
components.detail: `revAccept` saves the old work and books in 'rprev|<id>' (`REV_KEEP` = 7 days), moves the traces, installs the new package and reopens the text if open. `revReject` remembers the rejected version in 'revRej'. `revReturn` compares back, moves the traces again, writes the old records back with `revWrite` and rejects that revision. `revPrevLoad` drops kept versions older than 7 days.

mem: a full copy of the work while saving it
store: settings 'rprev|<id>': a full copy of the previous version for 7 days

components.name: Scriptorium
components.desc: The tab for your own reading: recently read works with where you stopped and a line of text, and works you annotated.
components.detail: Built from the recent-reading list (up to 60 entries, kept by the reader) and from your traces (glosses, markers, chosen analyses). Search and filters apply here too.

components.name: Recently read and Annotated
components.desc: Two sections: 'Recently read' and 'Annotated' (works with glosses, markers or chosen analyses not already under Recently read), 7 rows each at first.
components.detail: `scrLists` filters the recent list and the annotated works by search and filters, and orders annotated works by last opened and gloss count; `scrHTML` draws both sections with 'n of m shown', 'Show more' (+14) and an Edit mode to remove recent entries. `SCR_N` is the initial row count.

components.name: Scriptorium rows
components.desc: Each row shows title, author, where you are ('14.212'), the first words there, and the number of glosses.
components.detail: `scrRowHTML` draws the row (gloss count as a raised figure on narrow screens) with the download button or, in edit mode, a remove button; `posLabel` formats the position from the part label and section.

components.name: Works on this device
components.desc: Keeps downloaded works in their own database, one record per book, so only the open book is loaded; also handles removing, the 7-day bin and imported texts shown as works.
components.detail: Works live in IndexedDB 'greekreader-lib' with two stores, 'works' (metadata) and 'books' (the blocks of one reading unit, key '<id>|<n>'). Deleting a work moves a full copy into a settings record for 7 days so it can be restored offline. Imported texts (in 'greekreader') are wrapped by `impWork` to look like library works.

mem: est. a few MB: only the open book's blocks plus the work list
store: IndexedDB greekreader-lib: ~3.4x the .json.gz size per work (median ~90 kB, largest ~9.5 MB); all 2,547 works would be ~680 MB est.
cpu: package parsing on install; small reads otherwise

components.name: Open a book
components.desc: Loads just one book (part) of a work when the reader opens it.
components.detail: Library texts have ids 'w:<work id>:<book index>' (`isBook`). `loadBook` reads the work record and that one book's blocks and annotations, giving the reader a title 'Work · Book'. `openWork` opens the last book read in a work (setting 'wk|<id>') or the first.

mem: one book's blocks (typ. tens of kB to ~1 MB)

components.name: Library database
components.desc: Opens the on-device library database and reads works and books from it.
components.detail: `libDB` opens IndexedDB 'greekreader-lib' (version 1) once and keeps the connection in `libConn`; it creates the 'works' store (key 'id') and the 'books' store (key 'k' = '<work id>|<book index>'). `libGet` reads one record, `libWorks` reads all work records (used by the Library, search, maps and dialogs).

mem: one open connection; work list ~1 kB per installed work
store: IndexedDB greekreader-lib (see parent; up to hundreds of MB if many works are kept)

components.name: Imported texts as works
components.desc: Shows the user's own imported texts in the Library alongside downloaded works (source 'Imported').
components.detail: `impWork` turns a record of the 'texts' store into a work-like object with id 'imp:<n>', a language (stored or guessed by `detectLang`), a word count (regex over the text) and the author, date and notes typed on import. It is re-run over all imported texts whenever the Library opens or one changes.

mem: one small object per imported text
cpu: counts words of each imported text when the Library opens

components.name: Install and delete a work
components.desc: Writes a downloaded text package into the library database, or removes a work from it.
components.detail: `installWork` unpacks the package with `readPackage` (analysis.js), checks the format 'greekdict-work-1', clears any old books of the work and writes one 'books' record per part plus a 'works' record (author, titles, edition, source, licence, part labels, version, size, date, annotation lexicon) in one transaction. `deleteWork` removes the work and its books but keeps glosses and markers, so they return if the work is downloaded again; the open text is closed if it was this work.

mem: the whole unpacked package in memory while installing (largest ~9.5 MB JSON, more as objects est.)
cpu: gunzip + JSON parse + one write transaction, once per download (main thread)

components.name: Recently removed (7-day bin)
components.desc: A removed work or imported text is kept for 7 days and can be restored at once, even offline; after that it is erased for good.
components.detail: `trashWork` copies the work record and all its books into the settings record 'trash|<id>' before `deleteWork`; `trashImported` does the same for an imported text (with its Scriptorium entry). `workRestore` writes them back (`revWrite`) or puts the imported text back. `trashLoad` runs when the Library opens and drops entries older than 7 days; `workPurge` erases one at once. For erased imported texts `goneNote` keeps title and author ('gone|<key>') so their annotations can still be named.

mem: a full copy of the work in memory while moving it
store: settings store in greekreader: a full copy of each removed work for 7 days (doubles its size until erased)
cpu: copying all books of a work, on remove/restore

components.name: Date line
components.desc: A zoomable time line for choosing periods: the Library filter lists works whose author falls in the chosen periods, and Settings → Library sets its range, opening view and default periods.
components.detail: The same line is drawn in two places ('lib' in the filter panel, 'def' in Settings).
