It snaps to ten-year steps, shows era names that get finer when zoomed in, and supports tap, hold, drag, pinch, wheel and double-tap gestures. It is pure DOM; a canvas is only used to measure text widths.

cpu: DOM rebuild of the line on each pointer move while dragging

components.name: Drawing the line
components.desc: Draws the year ticks, the era names that fit, the chosen periods as pills with knobs, and the year labels while an end is pulled.
components.detail: `ftLineHTML` makes the empty frame; `ftDraw` fills it: 4-5 year ticks at a 'nice' step, era names (or their short forms) where they fit (widths from `ftTextW`, a cached canvas measure), eras touched by a period highlighted, periods as pills, and the pulled years (merged into one label when they would overlap, `ftLabel`). If the line is not laid out yet it retries up to 30 animation frames. `ftRender` draws both lines; `FTS` keeps the hovered period and labels per line.

cpu: rebuilds the line's HTML per pointer move while dragging

components.name: Era names
components.desc: Names the periods above the line (Bronze Age, Classical, Hellenistic … down to Flavian or Severan when zoomed in).
components.detail: `ERA_LV` holds three levels of eras: broad, middle and fine (fine gaps filled from the middle level); `ftLevel` picks one by the visible span (>3000 years, >400, else fine). `YMIN` (-800) and YMAX (1500) are the default range. `ERAS`, `eraOf` and `yPct` are left from the older century slider and are no longer used.

components.name: Touch and mouse gestures
components.desc: Tap the empty line for a first period, hold for another, pull ends, drag a period, hold it to split, pull two ends together to join, pinch or wheel to zoom, drag above/below to pan, double-tap for the default view.
components.detail: `wireDateLine` installs document-level pointer, wheel, dblclick and click listeners. It finds the nearest end within reach (14 px mouse, 30 px touch), snaps ends to 10-year steps (`ftSnap`, `FT_STEP`) and onto nearby ends, joins overlapping periods when let go, scrolls the line when an end is pulled past it, allows at most 6 periods, and uses a 550 ms hold timer and a short vibration as feedback. `FT_HELP`/`ftHelpHTML` give the help list shown in Settings.

cpu: per pointer move while dragging (redraws one line)

components.name: Settings → Library page
components.desc: The Library section of Settings: the date line's range, opening view and default periods, era names on/off, revision notices on/off and the list of rejected revisions.
components.detail: `libSettingsPrep` loads the revision settings, the view and the saved catalogue; `libSettingsHTML` builds the page with the 'def' date line and its help. The page's inputs are handled in `wireRevisions` (range checked: at most 100,000 BC-AD 2100 and at least a century; defaults and periods are cut to a new range).

components.name: The two lines
components.desc: Connects each line to what it changes: the Library's period filter, or the defaults in Settings.
components.detail: `FTC` gives, for 'lib' and 'def', where the periods live, the visible view and what happens after a change (the 'lib' line saves the view, updates the sieve and redraws the list; 'def' saves the settings). `ftLim` is the line's range (Settings, default 800 BC-AD 1500), `ftView0` the opening view and `ftView` the current one.

components.name: Typed years
components.desc: Understands years typed for the line's range in many styles: '500 BC', '-500', 'AD 120', '5th c. BC', 'late 5th century', '5. Jh. v. Chr.', 'saec. V', '2nd millennium BC'.
components.detail: `ftParseYear` normalises dashes and spaces, recognises BC/AD markers in English, German, Latin, French, Italian and Spanish (`FT_BC`, `FT_AD`), refuses BCE/CE and 'u. Z.' (`FT_NO`), handles circa, early/mid/late and first/second half of centuries and millennia (Roman numerals via `ftRoman`), and returns the first or last year. Wrong entries give undefined, empty ones null.

components.name: Page of a work
components.desc: A page per work: one line of facts, details on demand, the download button, Continue reading, the outline of parts and sections, and a search in the work with export.
components.detail: Opened from a row in the Library or the title button. For works not on the device it lists the parts and asks to download. Choosing a part or section opens it in the text behind the menu, which stays open and marks the place.

mem: outline tokens of the opened parts

components.name: Export of search results
components.desc: Saves the search results as PDF (print), HTML or Word, with each hit in its full sentence and the word in bold.
components.detail: `findDoc` makes the document (title, heading, groups); `findDocHTML` and `FIND_CSS` give the printable HTML (PDF through `printHTML`, HTML with the fonts inlined); `findDocx` writes a minimal .docx (document.xml with Gentium runs, zipped with `zipFiles`). The file is offered as a link to tap, because iPad downloads must start from a tap.

mem: the document blob (HTML with inlined fonts est. 1-3 MB)

components.name: Find in this work
components.desc: Searches all parts of a work for a word form (accents, case and j/v ignored, * as wildcard) or for a lemma (all forms of a dictionary headword); Latin letters also search as Greek.
components.detail: `findInWork` goes through the parts (`workParts`, `workPart`: tokens with annotations applied, or the open text's tokens), compares folded forms (`foldForm`) or, in lemma mode, the annotation's lemma or the lemmas from `analyses` (memoised per form), and stops at 2,000 hits. Each hit keeps its reference, a 13-word context and the sentence around it (`sentenceAt`, up to 30 words either side, `SENT_END`). `lmRunFind` runs it with progress shown every 150 ms.

mem: tokens of one part at a time + up to 2,000 hits
cpu: tokenises every part; lemma mode runs morphological analysis per distinct form; on the main thread

components.netNote: lemma mode uses the installed dictionaries

components.name: Work header and actions
components.desc: Shows title (as breadcrumb), Greek title, author, date, language and parts; ⓘ for edition, licence and notes; a ⋯ menu for favourites, the revision and editing/removing an imported text; and Continue reading.
components.detail: `lmWorkHTML` builds the page: the find field (when installed), the facts line, the download button, the ⋯ menu, notes on the 7-day bin or a failed download, 'Continue reading at 14.212' from the recent list, the revision notes (`revBackHTML`) and either the outline or the search results. `navFindFor` keeps the last search when coming back to the same work.

components.name: Outline of a work
components.desc: Parts › chapters › sections of any depth, with the path to the reading position unfolded and the current section marked; a tap opens that place.
components.detail: `outlineHTML` lists the parts (each unfolded on demand) and `outlineNodes` draws a tree level by level, showing the first words of each section and bookmark/pen signs only on the deepest visible row. `refTree` builds the tree from the reference list (verse lines numbered in fifties, Stephanus pages 227a as page › letter, '14.1.6' split on dots); `firstRef`/`treeHas` help find rows. `refsFor` gets a part's references (cached in `S.partRefCache`); `lmGoPlace` opens a place in the reader.

cpu: tokenises a part when it is first unfolded

components.name: Search results
components.desc: Shows the hits as a cut-down outline: groups by part (or chapter, or hundreds of lines), each unfolding to its places; a tap jumps there.
components.detail: `resultsHTML` shows the counts (for Latin letters, the Latin and the Greek search separately), up to 200 hits per group with 'Show more', and the Export/Outline buttons; groups unfold all when there are at most 30 hits. `findGroups`/`findGroup` group the hits.

components.name: Map
components.desc: The map of the ancient world: base map, layers, imagery, relief, sun and sky, drawing.

components.name: Drawing on the map
components.desc: Your own places, lines, arrows, areas, freehand lines and texts, in named sets, with lengths and areas, a period, and links to passages; GeoJSON in and out.
components.detail: Every drawing is one setting (`draw|<id>`, own places `pown|<id>`, sets `dset|<id>`) in IndexedDB, so it is saved immediately and included in backups. Drawings are MapLibre GeoJSON layers; their names, texts and lengths are HTML labels like the place names.

store: a few KB per drawing in settings
cpu: small; per frame while dragging points
gpu: a few line and fill layers

components.name: Drawings data
components.desc: Loads, saves and deletes drawings, own places and sets.
components.detail: `loadDrawings` reads all `draw|` and `dset|` settings once (creating the set 'My drawings' if there is none). `dSave`/`dRemove` write or delete a drawing or own place; `dGet`, `dSetOf`, `dKind` look them up; `dNewId`, `dClone`, `r5` (coordinates to 5 decimals) help; `D_KIND` names the kinds.

store: settings draw|, dset|, pown| in IndexedDB 'greekreader'

components.name: Selecting and changing drawings
components.desc: Tap a drawing to see its card; edit its name, note, set, colour, period and passages; drag, add or remove points; delete it.
components.detail: `tapDrawing` finds the drawing under a tap (labels, distance to segments, inside an area). `showDrawCard` shows kind, set, dates, length or area, note, linked passages and – with relief – a height profile. `dEditDialog` edits all properties (also turning a line into an arrow, adding the current section/chapter/book/work as a passage). `dHandles` places drag handles on the points, midpoints (to add a point) and the centre (to move all); `wireHandles` drags them (one update per frame), removes a point on a 550 ms hold, and records undo. `dDelete` asks and removes.

components.name: Drawings linked to passages
components.desc: A drawing linked to passages appears only while 'Places from' covers one of them.
components.detail: `dScopeUpdate` (run with every map refresh) computes which linked drawings to hide: `scopeCoverage` describes what 'Places from' covers now (section range, book, work, author's texts, selection) and `linkCovered` checks each link against it, reading other texts' references when needed (`workOfId`). `dGoLink` opens a linked passage from the card.

cpu: on each refresh, may read other texts

components.name: Lengths, areas and dates
components.desc: Measures lines and areas on the sphere and writes them in the chosen units.
components.detail: `havKm` (haversine; also used by the relief profile), `lenKm` and `areaKm2` (spherical polygon area as in GIS programs) measure; `fmtKm` gives the length in the chosen unit plus Roman miles and stades, `fmtArea`, `fmtN`, `dLenShort` format; `dMeasure` gives the card text. `dDates` and `parseYear` read and write a drawing's period ('401 BC', 'AD 117').

components.name: Drawing mode and tools
components.desc: The pen button's bar: tools (place, line, arrow, area, freehand, text, select), colour, width, dashes, set, undo and Done.
components.detail: `drawToggle` opens the bar (`drawBarHTML`, icons `D_TOOLS` made with the shared `svg` helper, `PEN_ICON`), disables double-click zoom and remembers the tool and style in `mapCfg`. `drawClick` takes taps on the map first: a place or text opens a name dialog (`dAddPoint`, `dAddText`), lines and areas collect points until the last/first point is tapped again (`dFinish` saves, `dTmp` shows the line in progress). `wireFreehand` draws with one finger (the map does not pan; a second finger cancels) and `simplify` (Douglas–Peucker, 1.4 px) thins the stroke. `dUndo` undoes points or whole saves; `dStyleSel` applies colour/width/dash also to the selected drawing; `dInfo` shows the chip with points and length; `drawUIClick` routes all buttons. Page-level code adds Esc, Enter and Ctrl+Z and the set/colour inputs.

cpu: per pointer move while drawing freehand

components.name: Drawing layers and labels
components.desc: Draws the drawings and your own places on the map, with names, texts and lengths.
components.detail: `drawStyle` adds the sources 'draw' and 'drawtmp' and layers for areas, a selection halo, solid and dashed lines, arrowheads and the line being drawn; `drawFC` turns the drawings into GeoJSON (arrowheads computed in screen pixels by `arrowHead`, so they are rebuilt on zoom); `ownFC` does the same for your own places. `dShown` hides switched-off sets and drawings whose passages are not covered; `dState`, `dOpacity`, `dTimeF` apply the period filter; `drawLayerProps` sets visibility and opacity. `drawLabelsOwn` writes names of own places, texts, names and lengths of lines as HTML labels and keeps their boxes for tapping.

cpu: labels per frame while moving; GeoJSON rebuilt on changes

components.name: Sets, import and export
components.desc: Named sets of drawings that can be shown or hidden, renamed, deleted, and exported or imported as GeoJSON.
components.detail: `ownLayersHTML` is the 'Your own' group of the layer menu (switch, sets with counts, new set, import, export all, lengths on/off). `dNewSet` creates a set; `dSetMenu` renames, exports or deletes one with its drawings. `dGeoJSON`/`dExport` write a FeatureCollection with simplestyle colours, lengths and areas (opens in QGIS, geojson.io …). `dImport` reads any GeoJSON (Multi* and collections split up, colours and Pult properties kept) into a new set and fits the map to it.

components.name: Map start-up and engine
components.desc: Opens the map pane: loads the map engine from the downloaded base package, builds the map and wires its controls; shows a clear message when something fails.
components.detail: The engine is MapLibre GL (version 5, or 4.7 for old downloads) read from 'pult-maps'; PMTiles packages are read straight out of the cache. Start-up runs in named steps with a 25 s watchdog so that a hang shows the step it stopped at. Map settings live in one object (`M.cfg`) saved as the setting `mapCfg`.

mem: MapLibre with its tile caches and GeoJSON sources (est. 100–250 MB on a large screen)
cpu: style building and tile parsing in workers
gpu: one WebGL canvas redrawn while moving

components.name: Map state and settings
components.desc: The shared map state and the map settings with their defaults and migrations.
components.detail: `M` is the one global object of the map (the place index, the MapLibre map, the selected place, hits, caches). `mapCfg` loads the setting `mapCfg` once, upgrades older settings (scope names, layer menu v5, retired base maps, sun and moon size) and merges it over the layer defaults `LCFG`; `saveMapCfg` writes it back. Also used by dialogs.js for backup and restore.

components.name: Loading MapLibre
components.desc: Loads the map engine from the base map package.
components.detail: `engineDir` picks `base/lib5/` (MapLibre 5) when it is in the cache, else `base/lib/` (4.7). `loadMapLib` adds the stylesheet and the script (version 5 is first patched by `shadePatchedLib` of maprelief.js), then pmtiles.js if present. `inCache` checks 'pult-maps'; `addScript` is a promise wrapper also used by maprelief.js; `mapLibP` makes it happen once.

store: engine files are part of the base package

components.name: Reading PMTiles from the cache
components.desc: Lets the map engine read tiles out of single-file packages kept in the cache.
components.detail: `pmInit` registers the `pmtiles://` protocol with MapLibre. `pmUrl` returns that address for a downloaded package file (landscape, Blue Marble, Itiner-e roads, relief) and registers a `CacheSource`, whose `getBytes` slices the requested byte range out of the cached Blob (`pmBlob`, one Blob per file kept for the session).

mem: Blob handles per package file; tile bytes sliced on demand

components.name: Map scripts check
components.desc: Makes sure the map's script files have run before the map starts.
components.detail: `ensureMapScripts` checks that maplayers.js, mapsaved.js, mapdraw.js and maprelief.js defined their main functions; a missing one is loaded once more from the website with a cache-busting query. Script errors of map files are collected in `SCRIPT_ERR` (by a global error listener) and shown if the map cannot start.
components.netNote: reloading a missing script needs the network

components.name: Opening the map
components.desc: Builds the map pane and the MapLibre map, step by step, or says why it could not.
components.detail: `showMap` runs `showMap1` once at a time with a 25 s watchdog. `showMap1` checks the base package, collects the files of installed and switched-on packages, loads the ancient labels, the full gazetteer and the drawings, writes the pane's HTML (buttons, time bar, card, pop-up), loads the engine, imagery catalogues and relief, then creates the `maplibregl.Map` (globe, pitch up to 85°, zoom 0–16) at the last position (`mpos|last`). It hooks map events: labels on every move (one per frame), fewer dots when zoomed out, saving the position, taps (picking a point, drawing, places, drawings, roads, rivers), WebGL context loss. `mapFailed` shows the error with 'Try again', 'Reset the map settings' (old settings kept as `mapCfgOld`) and 'Use the previous map engine'.

mem: the MapLibre map and its sources (est. 100–250 MB)
cpu: building the style and first tiles

components.name: Map tab and controls
components.desc: The map button in the toolbar, and the dispatcher for all buttons inside the map pane.
components.detail: The toolbar button shows a small Mediterranean image (`EUROPE_ICON`); tapping toggles the map (`toggleMapTab`), holding opens Settings → Map. `wireMapUI` wires one click handler on the map pane that routes to the card, corrections, the check list, 'Places from', layers, saved maps, drawing, relief and globe menus, and one input handler for the gazetteer search. The page-level code of maps.js also blocks page zoom gestures over the map, handles package switches and 'Rebuild place index' in Instruments, the dictionary's map button and the display switches of the map settings.

components.name: Globe, flat map and 3D
components.desc: Switches between globe and flat (Mercator) projection and turns 3D terrain on or off.
components.detail: `viewOn` reads `cfg.globe`/`cfg.t3d` (both on by default). `viewToggle` sets the projection or the terrain (`T3D`: source 'terrdem' with the reader's exaggeration, default 1.5) without moving the camera, and updates the obelisk shadow. `mapPt` projects a point to the screen and, on the zoomed-out globe, moves points on the far side off screen so their labels are not drawn.

gpu: 3D terrain adds mesh work per frame

components.name: Gazetteer (place index)
components.desc: The ancient places of the Pleiades gazetteer (~34,500 places), indexed on the device so names in texts can be looked up fast.
components.detail: The index is built once from `places/places.json` of the 'places' package and kept in its own IndexedDB 'pult-places'. Reading a text loads only the name bundles and places it needs; opening the map loads every place. Each place gets a significance rank 0–9 that decides which dots and names show when zoomed out.

mem: all places as objects while the map is open (est. 20–40 MB)
cpu: building the index once takes seconds

components.name: Building the index
components.desc: Turns the downloaded gazetteer file into the on-device index.
components.detail: `buildPlaceIndex` fetches `maps/places/places.json` (3.7 MB, served from 'pult-maps' by the service worker), turns 34,463 rows into place objects, corrects start dates from titles ('Late Roman province' → AD 284), and collects exact-name keys and stem keys for the Greek, Latin and romanised names; stem keys only for main kinds of places (`MAIN_TYPES`), and generic first words like 'Ager' or 'Mons' are skipped (`GENERIC`). It ranks the places, then writes all bundles in transactions of 4,000. It runs after the package is installed or updated, on 'Rebuild place index', or when first needed.

mem: whole JSON parsed plus two key maps (est. 40–80 MB briefly)
cpu: once, several seconds on a phone (est.)

components.name: Place database
components.desc: The IndexedDB 'pult-places' where the place index lives, read in bundles.
components.detail: `plDB` opens 'pult-places' with four stores: p (places, in bundles of 512 = `PB`), k (name keys, hashed by `plHash` into 1,024 bundles), id (place id → number, 512 bundles) and meta (info, ranks). Bundling makes writing a few hundred large records much faster than 100,000 small ones. `plGet`/`plGetMany` read records; `plKey` keeps up to ~1,100 recently read name bundles in memory; `placeIndexInfo` reads the build info; `dropPlaceIndex` clears everything (when the package is deleted).

mem: cached name bundles (est. a few MB)

components.name: Name keys
components.desc: Normalises Greek and Latin names so that different spellings and endings meet.
components.detail: `translit` turns Greek letters into the Latin spelling used by the gazetteer (rough breathing → h, γγ → ng, diphthongs). `exKey` is the exact key (the app's `gkey`). `stemKey` merges spelling variants (ae/e, k/c, ph/f, y/i, double letters) and strips common case endings, keeping at least three letters.

components.name: Loading places
components.desc: Brings places from the database into memory: only those needed while reading, all of them for the map.
components.detail: `loadPlaceIndex(full)` rebuilds the index if the package version changed, then either loads every place bundle (`getAll`) for the map or starts an empty table for reading; it also loads your own places (`pown|` settings). `placesLoad` and `placesLoadIds` fetch single bundles on demand and drop the rest of each bundle. `placeById` also finds your own places ('o…' ids); `hasType`, `isRegion`, `isPeople`, `isWater` and `typeLabel` classify a place by its gazetteer types.

mem: all ~34,500 place objects with the map open (est. 20–40 MB)
cpu: loading all bundles when the map opens

components.name: Significance of places
components.desc: Gives every place a rank 0–9 so that zoomed out only the important places get dots and names.
components.detail: `placeScore` weighs links from other places, population, mentions in the library and on this device, number of names, city status, having both Greek and Latin names, and a penalty for rough positions (`SIG_DEF`, adjustable with sliders `SIG_UI` in the map settings). `rankPlaces` sorts by score and hands out ranks by position (top 30 → 9, next 50 → 8 … `RANK_TOP`), then saves the ranks to 'pult-places' after 1.5 s. `storeCounts`/`loadDevCounts` keep per-text counts (`pcnt|`), and `countDevice` reads every text on the device to count them; `recomputeSig` re-ranks and refreshes the dots.

mem: a score array for all places
store: ranks in 'pult-places', a count per text in settings
cpu: sorting 34,500 places on each weight change; 'Count the places in all texts' reads every text (minutes, est.)

components.name: Searching the gazetteer
components.desc: Finds places by name while correcting a place on the map.
components.detail: `searchPlaces` loads the whole gazetteer if needed, then scans all places for names starting with the typed text (exact key) or with the same stem, stopping after 31 hits. It runs 200 ms after typing stops.

cpu: a linear scan of ~34,500 places per search

components.name: Globe menu
components.desc: The map's 'Globe' menu: globe or flat, 3D, compass, imagery and its version, height exaggeration, elevation, shading, contour lines and spacing, Save relief, rivers and lakes.
components.detail: `mapOptsHTML` builds it from the map settings and `mapOptsPop` opens it in the right-hand popup; `mapOptsClick` handles its buttons and also the sundial's (open, Sun/Moon, Here, page swap, date style, mode, play/pause). Projection and 3D toggles animate the icon first and change the map a frame later. The icons are drawn in code: `projIconSVG` morphs a globe (`PROJ_LINES`, `projPt`, `projD`) into a Mercator rectangle, `hillIconSVG`/`chapelSVG` lift the Wurmlinger Berg's contour rings into 3D (`HILL`, `HILL_LIFT`), `iconAnim` eases between shapes over 0.45 s. `compassUpd` turns the compass needle against the map's bearing. Note: the menu sits in mapsun.js but concerns the whole map, not only relief.

cpu: about 27 SVG rebuilds during a 0.45 s icon animation

components.name: Imagery and online waters
components.desc: Photographic base maps (NASA Blue Marble offline; Sentinel-2 and Esri online) and, online, the rivers and lakes of OpenStreetMap.
components.detail: Blue Marble from the base package always lies beneath any online imagery, so gaps show Blue Marble instead of nothing; going offline or online rebuilds the style.

mem: raster tile textures in MapLibre's cache (est. 20–60 MB)
store: Blue Marble 15.8 MB in the base package; catalogues in settings

components.netNote: Blue Marble offline from the package; Sentinel-2, Esri, NASA tiles to zoom 8 and OSM rivers online

components.name: Imagery versions
components.desc: Keeps the list of Sentinel-2 years and Esri Wayback dates the reader can choose from.
components.detail: `imgInit` loads the ArcGIS key and the saved catalogue (`imgCat`) and, online, refreshes it at most once a week in the background: `imgCatalogs` reads EOX's WMS capabilities (`EOX_CAPS`) for the s2cloudless years and Esri's Wayback configuration (`WAYBACK_CFG`) for the capture dates. `s2Versions` falls back to a built-in list (`S2_DEF`, 2016, 2018–2024); `waybackVersions` gives the dates (used by the globe menu).
components.netNote: refreshed online once a week; the saved list offline

components.name: Imagery layers and credits
components.desc: Places the imagery beneath waters, lines and names, and shows the required credits on the map.
components.detail: `imgStyle` inserts the Blue Marble layer and the online layer below the ancient waters/areas or lakes, and adds lake outlines on top (from zoom 5 those of the landscape package). `imgLayerProps` hides the drawn land, sea, lakes and the relief's sea floor and colours while imagery is on. `imgPaint` sets a short fade and linear resampling. `imgCredit` writes the Sentinel-2 / Esri (with Wayback date) and OpenStreetMap credits into the corner.

mem: raster tiles in MapLibre's tile cache
gpu: one or two full-screen raster layers

components.name: Online/offline switching
components.desc: Rebuilds the map's style when the device goes online or offline, or when the imagery choice or the ArcGIS key changes.
components.detail: On the browser's online and offline events `netRelief` re-initialises the relief (Mapterhorn online, packages offline) and then `imgNetChange` rebuilds the style and refreshes places and credits. The page-level code of mapimg.js also handles the imagery select boxes, the ArcGIS key field (kept on this device only) and the river look controls.

cpu: a full style rebuild on each switch

components.name: Rivers and lakes from OpenStreetMap
components.desc: Online, draws rivers, streams, canals and lakes from OpenStreetMap at every zoom; offline the base map's own waters are used.
components.detail: `rivStyle` adds the OpenFreeMap planet vector tiles (`OFM`, OpenMapTiles schema) as 'osm-lakes' and 'osm-rivers' (no tunnels), and gives the offline rivers the same colour and width factor. `rivPaint` colours by kind from strongest (rivers) to weakest (streams) with widths by zoom; `scaleW` scales width stops. `rivLayerProps` hides the offline waters while OSM is shown. `rivSettingsHTML` and `rivRepaint` handle width and colour settings (`RIV_DEF`, `rivCfg`); `osmRiv` says whether OSM is used.
components.netNote: OSM waters online only; Natural Earth/landscape waters offline

components.name: Imagery sources
components.desc: Decides which imagery is shown and where its tiles come from.
components.detail: `imgKind` is the reader's choice (Blue Marble, Sentinel-2 or Esri). `imgOnline` returns the online raster source: NASA GIBS Blue Marble to zoom 8 (`GIBS_BM`), EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless by year via WMS (`EOX_WMS`, to zoom 15), or Esri World Imagery – current with a free ArcGIS key (`ESRI_CUR`) or an earlier Wayback capture (to zoom 19). `bmPkg` gives the Blue Marble PMTiles of the base package (`BM_PKG`); `imgOn` says whether any imagery can be shown; `isOnline` reads `navigator.onLine` (also used by relief and sun).
components.netNote: online sources need the network; the package works offline

components.name: River and lake card
components.desc: A tap on an OpenStreetMap river or lake shows its names and kind.
components.detail: `waterTap` queries the OSM water layers within a fingertip, prefers a named feature, and shows the name with its Latin, English, Greek or local variants, the kind (`RIV_KIND`), whether it dries up at times or crosses on a bridge.
components.netNote: only while the OSM waters are shown (online)

components.name: Layers
components.desc: Everything the map can show on top of the base map – all gazetteer places by kind, the ancient world, roads, names of regions – and the Layers menu that switches them.
components.detail: `layerStyle` assembles one MapLibre style from the base map and the layers of every module (imagery, rivers, drawings, relief, sun), and `layerProps`/`applyLayers` set visibility, filters and opacity from the settings and the period filter.

mem: GeoJSON sources of the ancient world (~4 MB files) and 34,500 site points
cpu: re-applying filters on every period change

components.name: Layers menu
components.desc: The menu of the layers button: Places, Political, Built world, Names on the map, Your own – folded groups with counts of what is on.
components.detail: `layersHTML` builds the groups with toggles (`tgl`), segmented choices (`segc`) and fold sections (`foldSec`, fold state remembered), showing 'Needs the download …' where a package is missing. `rightPop` shows such a menu at the right side of the map and remembers its scroll position (also used by the relief and globe menus); `layersPop` opens it, `refreshLayersPop` re-renders it after a change. `layerClick`/`layerClick1` handle every button of the menu, the period buttons and the map settings: changing a value saves `mapCfg` and either re-applies the layers or rebuilds the style (units, base map, imagery).

cpu: on taps; a style rebuild for some settings

components.name: Names of regions, peoples and sites
components.desc: Writes the names of regions, peoples, mountains, islands and seas along their lines, and the names of all places when every place is shown.
components.detail: `loadAncientLabels` reads `ancient/labels.json` (0.5 MB) once and keeps, for each label, its longest line, end points and bounding box. `moreLabels` (called by `drawLabels`) places up to 160 of those in view, longest first, rotated along their line with letter spacing, faded by the period filter and coloured by period if chosen; then, with 'Places from' off, up to 180 site names from the rendered dots, biggest rank first, smaller and fainter when zoomed out.

cpu: once per frame while moving (text measuring, rendered-feature query)

components.name: Roman road card
components.desc: A tap on a road of Itiner-e shows what is known of it.
components.detail: `roadTap` queries the three Itiner-e road layers within a fingertip and fills the card with the road's name, main or secondary, certainty of the course, dates, the itineraries naming it and its builder (Itiner-e, CC BY 4.0).

components.name: Map settings
components.desc: The map settings (hold the map button, or ☰ → Settings → Map): display, units, places in texts, period options, significance weights.
components.detail: `settingsHTML` builds the section: scale bar, zoom level, size of sun and moon, the look of rivers, the ArcGIS key, units, jumping to places, persons, names, tolerance, how faded/hidden things show, period colours, slider range and default view, significance sliders and 'Count the places in all texts'. `mapSettingsDialog` shows it as a dialog; dialogs.js also embeds it. The page-level code of maplayers.js handles its inputs (default view, slider range, period colours, weights) and closes map menus on a tap outside.

components.name: All places by kind
components.desc: With 'Places from' switched off, shows every place of the gazetteer as a coloured dot by kind (settlements, sanctuaries, forts …).
components.detail: `sitesData` turns every place (except purely modern ones) into a GeoJSON point with its category (`SITE_CATS`, 11 kinds with light and dark colours), rank and dates, cached as `M.sitesFC`. `siteCats` gives the kinds ticked in the menu (settlements by default); `dotMinW` hides less significant dots when zoomed out (rank ≥7 below zoom 3.5 … all from 6.5); `siteFont` sizes names by rank.

mem: a 34,500-point GeoJSON source and its tiles (est. 10–20 MB)
cpu: tiling the points in a worker on each setData

components.name: Style assembly
components.desc: Puts all layers into one map style and keeps their visibility, filters and opacity in step with the settings.
components.detail: `layerStyle` adds: the detailed landscape (PMTiles; exact coasts, lakes and rivers from zoom 5, inside 20°W–80°E, 0–62°N), the ancient-world layers (coastline of the period, areas of regions and peoples, empires with colours `EMP_COL`, provinces, roads, canals, aqueducts, walls, city outlines), Itiner-e roads (certain solid, conjectured dashed, hypothetical dotted), your own places, drawings, the all-places dots, then imagery, OSM rivers, relief and sun. `layerProps` computes for each layer id its visibility, filter and paint from `M.cfg` and the period filter (Barrington roads hide when Itiner-e is installed); `applyLayersTo` applies them before the style is built, `applyLayers` on the live map (and redraws labels).

mem: parsed GeoJSON sources (ancient roads 2 MB, empires 0.6 MB …)
cpu: rebuilding the style; applyLayers on every change

components.name: Obelisk
components.desc: An obelisk of red porphyry the reader can set on the map ('Here'): the sundial then reads that place, and the obelisk casts a real shadow away from the sun - long at dusk, none at night.
components.detail: Drawn with three.js as a custom layer in the map's WebGL (with a soft stencil shadow on flat ground) when three.js loads; otherwise, and for the shadow on 3D terrain or very long shadows, with the map engine's own extruded blocks and a ground polygon. Its height is fixed in metres when set (then it grows as one zooms in), times the reader's size ⅓-3×; it can be dragged.
components.netNote: three.js fetched once, then cached; the block version works offline anyway

components.name: Obelisk from map blocks and its ground shadow
components.desc: Draws the obelisk with the map engine's own extruded blocks, and its shadow laid on the ground away from the sun - used when three.js is unavailable, and for the shadow on 3D terrain or long shadows on the globe.
components.detail: `obelGeo` fixes the height in metres when set (`OB_H` = 34 screen px at that zoom, times the reader's size `obelK` ⅓-3×), builds 32 stacked square extrusions (plinth, 20-step tapering shaft, 10-step point) in porphyry colours dimmed at dusk/night, and sets `self.__pultObLight` for the engine patch. The shadow is three overlapping polygons along great circles from the foot, length H/tan(altitude) capped at 8H, opacity by altitude; none at night. `obelUpd` creates/updates the `obel`/`obelsh` sources and layers (or removes them), and decides whether the three.js model draws instead; `obelShadow` refreshes after a size change.

store: code only (part of the app files)

components.name: Obelisk 3D model (three.js)
components.desc: Draws a realistic red-porphyry obelisk with three.js inside the map, lit by the sun where it stands and casting a soft shadow on flat ground.
components.detail: `threeLib` imports three.js 0.169 once from `lib/` (cached by the offline helper in 'pult-lib'); on failure the map blocks stand in. `porphyryTex` paints a 256 px speckled stone texture. `obel3dLayer` is a MapLibre custom layer sharing the map's WebGL context: plinth boxes, a square frustum shaft and a pyramid point with standard materials, a directional sun light (warmer when low, dimmer at dusk) and a hemisphere sky light. It draws after the map's frame (on `render`) so it covers the atmosphere glow but is still hidden by hills; on flat ground the shadow is five stencil-masked projections from slightly shifted suns, giving soft edges.
components.netNote: three.js is fetched on first use, then cached for offline

mem: three.js module (~0.7 MB code, several MB parsed) plus a small scene and texture
cpu: per map frame: matrices and a small scene render
gpu: 6 draws (×5 shadow copies) with standard materials per frame

components.name: Placing and dragging the obelisk
components.desc: 'Here' sets an obelisk on the map at the next tap (and takes it away again); the obelisk can then be dragged with a finger or the mouse.
components.detail: `sunHere` toggles `mapCfg.gnomon` ({lng, lat, h}), saved with the map settings; while set, the dial, shading direction and sky use that place. `obelDragHook` catches pointer events in the capture phase before the map engine, hit-testing the 3D model's projected axis (`obel3dAxis`) or the fill-extrusion features and the foot, then moves the obelisk on every pointer move and blocks map panning meanwhile.

components.name: Map packages
components.desc: Downloads, updates, switches off and deletes the optional map packages (base map, landscape, ancient world, gazetteer, roads) in ☰ → Instruments → Map.
components.detail: The list of packages comes from `maps/maps.json`; the files themselves come from the lesepult-maps site and are kept whole in the Cache 'pult-maps', where the service worker serves them as ordinary `maps/…` addresses. Installed versions and switched-off packages are remembered in the settings (`mapPk`, `mapOff`). Only 'Base map' is required; packages with two levels of detail are one row with a choice, and installing one level removes the other.

mem: a downloaded file is joined in memory before it is stored (up to ~40 MB for the largest)
store: Cache 'pult-maps': ~21 MB base map, +25 MB landscape, +7–39 MB roads, ~4 MB each for gazetteer and ancient layers

components.netNote: downloading needs the network; installed packages work offline

components.name: Download and delete
components.desc: Fetches a package file by file, resumes broken downloads, and removes packages again.
components.detail: `downloadMapPkg` fetches every file from the package's own address (lesepult-maps), up to three tries each; big files come as numbered parts that are parked in Cache 'pult-dl-parts' (tagged with the version) so a stopped download continues where it broke off, then joined into one Blob and stored in 'pult-maps'. Afterwards the other level of the same group is deleted, the gazetteer index is rebuilt for 'places', and the map is rebuilt if its style changes. `downloadMapQueued` is the entry used by the download queue of dialogs.js (progress on the row's button). `deleteMapPkg` keeps files that another installed package still uses.

mem: parts of one file held as Blobs and joined (up to ~40 MB, est.)

components.netNote: needs the network to download; deleting works offline

components.name: Package list and status
components.desc: Knows which map packages exist, which are installed and which are switched off.
components.detail: `mapManifest` fetches `maps/maps.json` (6 s time-out) and keeps a copy in 'pult-maps', falling back to that copy offline. `mapInstalled` reads the setting `mapPk` (and migrates the old 'ancient' package into its two halves); `mapOff` reads `mapOff`; `mapHas` combines both. `mapsEnabled` always answers yes now (the map can no longer be switched off as a whole). `MAPS` also names the cache 'pult-maps' (MAPCACHE).

store: maps.json copy in 'pult-maps', two small settings

components.netNote: fresh list online; the cached list offline

components.name: Instruments → Map section
components.desc: The rows of map packages in the Instruments dialog, with level choices, switches and 'Rebuild place index'.
components.detail: `mapSectionHTML` groups the manifest into Basic / Appearance / Gazetteers (`MAP_GROUPS`), folds regional packages, hides retired packages unless still installed, and appends the saved relief areas of maprelief.js. `redrawMapSection` re-renders it in place keeping the scroll position; `mapSummary` gives the 'n packages installed' line. When a package is switched on or off, `mapPkChanged` throws the map away and rebuilds it (and the places of the text for 'places'); `applyMapsOn` shows or hides the map tab button.

components.name: Relief
components.desc: The landscape on the map: hillshade shading (lit by the real sun when sunlight is on), colours by height, sea depths, contour lines with numbers, heights and profiles, and relief saved for offline use.
components.detail: Elevation comes from Mapterhorn's 512 px Terrarium WebP tiles (zoom 0-12), read by the map engine and by maplibre-contour (contour lines, in its own worker) from the same addresses. Areas saved from the Globe menu go into the 'pult-relief' cache; the offline helper (reliefsw.js) serves them, online too, and offline enlarges coarser saved tiles when zooming deeper. maprelief.js also patches the map engine's code as it loads (shading by the sun, obelisk light), and mapsun.js holds the Globe menu that switches these layers. Without a connection and without saved areas, relief is off.
components.netNote: online anywhere; offline only in saved areas

mem: engine DEM textures + contour worker cache + service-worker enlarge cache (est. 30-100 MB)
store: saved areas in Cache 'pult-relief': MB to GB
cpu: contour generation in a worker; tile enlarging in the service worker; downloads
gpu: hillshade and colour-relief shaders every frame

components.name: Contour spacing and numbers
components.desc: Lets the reader space contour lines closer or wider, and writes their height numbers with a font made on the device.
components.detail: `contSpacing` returns the reader's least room between lines (4-24 CSS px, default 9); `reliefStyle` scales its thresholds by it and rounds to 'nice' steps (10, 20, 25, 50 …); a change rebuilds the style after 0.5 s. For the numbers, `glyphInit` registers a `pultglyph://` protocol with MapLibre (the style's glyph URL points there). `pultGlyphs` renders only digits, comma, point, minus and space once with TinySDF from the app's 'Source Sans 3', and `pbfGlyphs` hand-encodes them as a protocol-buffer glyph file (varints, zig-zag) for range 0-255; other ranges get an empty answer. No glyph server is needed, so labels work offline.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: glyphs once; contour regeneration after a spacing change
gpu: labels drawn by the engine's symbol shader

components.name: Map engine patches (sun shading, obelisk light)
components.desc: Changes the map engine as it loads so the relief is shaded by the real sun at every point, the night side is unshaded, and the block obelisk is lit by its own sun.
components.detail: `SHADE_PATCH` is a list of exact text replacements in MapLibre 5.24's minified code: new uniforms for the tile's longitude range and the sun (`self.__pultSun` = sin/cos of declination, subsolar longitude, on/off), per-pixel solar azimuth and altitude in the hillshade fragment shader, and a smoothstep fade around sunset. `OB_PATCH` makes fill-extrusions use `self.__pultObLight` (position, intensity) instead of the atmosphere light. `shadePatchedLib` fetches the engine script, applies each group with `enginePatch` (every search string must occur the expected number of times, else the group is skipped whole) and loads the result from a Blob URL; with another engine version it loads unchanged and shading falls back to one direction (`M.shadePatch` = false).

mem: a second copy of the engine source (~1 MB) as a Blob
store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: string replacements once at map start
gpu: a few extra shader instructions per hillshade pixel

components.name: Heights and elevation profiles
components.desc: Gives the elevation of a tapped place (on the place card) and a height profile with climb and descent for a drawn line or shape.
components.detail: `heightAt` converts a position to the Mapterhorn tile at the requested zoom (max 12), asks the shared DemSource for the decoded tile (`getDemTile`) and returns the nearest pixel's height in metres, or null without relief. `profileOf` walks a line by great-circle distance (`havKm`) and samples 121 heights at zoom 8, 10 or 11 depending on length. `profileSVG` draws them as a filled SVG curve (280 × 64) and sums total climb and descent in the map's length units.
components.netNote: offline only inside saved areas (or enlarged from coarser saved tiles)

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: up to 121 sequential tile lookups per profile

components.name: Shading, height colours, sea depths and contour layers
components.desc: Adds the relief layers to the map: hillshade shading, colours by height, sea depths and contour lines, each switchable.
components.detail: `reliefStyle` is called by the layer builder whenever the style is rebuilt. It adds Natural Earth sea depths (`rel-bathy`, from the installed map package's `relief/bathy.pmtiles`, 5 depth bands, fading out under detailed coasts), raster-dem sources on Mapterhorn (`reldem`, plus `terrdem` for 3D terrain), a `color-relief` layer (MapLibre 5 only, checked by `engineMajor`) and a darken-only black `hillshade` whose exaggeration falls with zoom. It defines the contour source through maplibre-contour's protocol URL (thresholds per zoom in metres or feet, scaled by the reader's spacing) and three layers: thin orange lines, the 0 m coast line, and numbered labels in the font stack 'Pult'. `REL_DEF`/`relOn` give each switch's default (shading on, colours off, contours on, sea depths on) and `reliefLayerProps` returns the layers' visibility, applied without rebuilding the style.
components.netNote: tiles from Mapterhorn online, from saved areas offline; sea depths need the map package

mem: engine DEM textures for visible tiles (512 px each, est. 10-40 MB) plus contour vector tiles
store: code only; tiles cached by the engine and the offline helper
cpu: contour generation in maplibre-contour's worker as tiles arrive
gpu: hillshade and color-relief shaders over the whole map every frame

components.name: Relief tile server (offline helper)
components.desc: Inside the offline helper, answers every Mapterhorn tile request: from saved areas first, then the network, and offline - deeper than an area was saved - by enlarging the nearest coarser saved tile.
components.detail: `reliefServe` (called by sw.js for tiles.mapterhorn.com) returns a cached tile if present, else fetches with an 8 s timeout (network-only, 30 s, for `?pult-save` requests from the downloader). Failing that, it looks up through coarser zooms for a saved ancestor and enlarges it, keeping up to 48 results in memory (`self.relMem`). `decodeDem` decodes WebP to Terrarium heights; `noisyCanvas` detects browsers that randomise canvas reads (one red step = 256 m) and then `framePixels` reads pixels through a `VideoFrame` instead. `enlargeDem` resamples the sub-square bilinearly to 512 px (smooth, not real detail), and `encodeDem` writes a Terrarium PNG with stored (uncompressed) deflate (`zlib`, Adler-32) and CRC-32 chunks (`pngChunk`, `CRC`) - compression would save ~10 % but cost 5× the time.
components.netNote: cache first, network second, enlargement when offline

mem: up to 48 enlarged tiles of ~0.8 MB (uncompressed PNG) in the service worker, plus ~1 MB float grids while enlarging (est. ~40 MB)
cpu: per enlarged tile: decode + 262,144 bilinear samples + PNG write, in the service worker

components.name: Save relief offline
components.desc: The 'Save relief offline' panel from the Globe menu: pick the detail, see the size, name the area and download its elevation tiles to the device.
components.detail: `viewArea` takes the area on screen (the whole world when the globe is wholly visible), `areaRanges`/`areaCount` list its Web-Mercator tiles for every zoom up to the chosen one (two ranges across 180°), and `mPerPx`/`fmtM`/`fmtBytes`/`areaKm`/`coordName` make that readable. `reliefSavePop`/`reliefSaveHTML`/`reliefSaveInfo` show the form (default detail: deepest zoom under 3,000 tiles; cap `RS_MAX_TILES` = 400,000) with a size estimate from five sample tiles (`areaSample`) and free storage, and a name from Nominatim (`areaName`, continents via `CONT`). `reliefSave` asks for persistent storage and runs six parallel workers over all (z, x, y): tiles already cached by another area are counted, not fetched; each fetch is retried 3 times; sizes are kept in an `x-size` header. Progress is saved every 5 s; Stop, or 50 failures, ends the job, which can be resumed later. Saving continues only while Pult is open.
components.netNote: needs Mapterhorn (tiles, size estimate) and Nominatim (name; falls back to coordinates)

store: Cache 'pult-relief': up to 400,000 WebP tiles per area - from a few MB to several GB
cpu: network-bound, six parallel requests; UI updated at most every 300 ms

components.name: Saved relief areas
components.desc: Keeps the list of saved relief areas and shows it in Settings → Maps, with Resume and Delete.
components.detail: The list (`[{id, name, w, s, e, n, z, world, total, tiles, bytes, at, state}]`) is a JSON entry `pult-relief-areas.json` in the same cache as the tiles ('pult-relief'), read once by `reliefAreas` and written by `putAreas`. `reliefAreasHTML` renders it with detail, size, date and state (saving %, incomplete %). `reliefDelete` stops a running job and deletes only tiles no remaining area covers (`areaHas`, scanning all cache keys); offline with nothing left, relief is turned off. The script's top-level listeners handle Resume/Delete clicks and the save form's detail slider and name field.

store: one small JSON entry; deleting frees relief cache space
cpu: scans every cached tile key on delete

components.name: Elevation source
components.desc: Connects the map to Mapterhorn's elevation tiles so that shading, colours by height, contour lines, 3D and heights can be drawn.
components.detail: `reliefInit` runs while the map is built: online it always turns relief on; offline only if at least one area was saved (else `M.rel`/`M.relDem` stay null and every relief feature is off). It loads maplibre-contour on demand (`addScript`) and creates one shared `mlcontour.DemSource` (Terrarium WebP, 512 px, zoom 0-12, decoding in a worker, cache of 24 tiles, 30 s timeout). `MH_URL`/`mhTileUrl` hold the Mapterhorn address pattern; the engine, maplibre-contour and the offline save all use the same addresses, so the offline helper can answer them from one cache.
components.netNote: online: any place; offline: only inside areas saved beforehand

mem: DemSource worker cache of up to 24 decoded 512 px DEM tiles (~1 MB each, est. ~25 MB)
store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: tile decoding in maplibre-contour's worker, off the main thread

components.name: Saved maps and export
components.desc: Saves what the map shows to open again later, and exports it as an image, a PDF or a Pult map file.
components.detail: A saved map is one setting `mmap|<id>`: texts, part, view, periods and layer settings. Exports are made on the device and offered as a file to save.

mem: a full-resolution canvas copy while exporting (est. 10–40 MB)
cpu: drawing labels and encoding PNG/JPEG on export

components.name: Export
components.desc: Exports the map as PNG, PDF or a Pult map file with its places and corrections.
components.detail: `exportMap` names the file from `mapTitle` (work, part and periods). For a Pult map file it bundles the map state, the places shown and all corrections, own places, drawings and sets that belong to the texts (JSON 'pult-map-1'); for PNG/PDF it renders the image. The result is offered through the app's save-file dialog.

components.name: Opening a map file
components.desc: Opens a Pult map file, adding its corrections, own places and drawings, and shows the map.
components.detail: `importMapFile` checks the format 'pult-map-1', asks for confirmation, writes the contained `pl|`, `plw|`, `plg|`, `pown|`, `draw|`, `dset|` settings (replacing yours where they differ), saves the map and opens it. The texts must be in the library.

components.name: Map image
components.desc: Draws the map as it is on screen, with its labels, a title and the credits, into one picture.
components.detail: `mapCanvas` waits for one map render, copies the WebGL canvas at device resolution, then redraws every HTML label onto it (font, opacity, letter spacing, rotation, a halo in the background colour), adds a 46 px footer with the title and the credits of the layers actually visible (Pleiades, imagery, Natural Earth, OSM, AWMC, Itiner-e, Mapterhorn). Also used by the sun module.

mem: a canvas of screen size × device pixel ratio (est. 10–30 MB)

components.name: Saved maps menu
components.desc: The bookmark button's menu: the saved maps, save, open a map file, export.
components.detail: `savePop` lists the saved maps with delete buttons and the export choices (Image, PDF, Pult map file); `savedClick` handles its buttons and those of the 'Places from' menu and selection editor (switch, edit, add, remove, browse, show).

components.name: PDF writer
components.desc: Wraps the map picture into a one-page A4 landscape PDF.
components.detail: `pdfOf` encodes the canvas as JPEG (quality 0.92) and writes a minimal PDF 1.4 by hand: catalog, page, one image XObject with DCTDecode, a content stream fitting it with 24 pt margins, and the cross-reference table. No PDF library is needed.

components.name: Saving and opening maps
components.desc: Saves the current map under a name and opens a saved one again.
components.detail: `mapState` records the scope, open text and reference, centre and zoom, the period ranges and the layer settings listed in `MAP_KEYS`. `saveMapDialog` suggests a name and stores it as `mmap|<id>`; `savedMaps` lists them newest first. `openSavedMap` opens the text and passage if needed, restores the settings (rebuilding the style if the base map differs), periods, view, and refreshes.

components.name: Sky
components.desc: Behind the globe and above the horizon of a tilted view, a sky in the manner of Flammarion's 1888 engraving: real stars and the zodiac's lines turning with the sky, and the sun and moon where they truly stand, the moon in its real phase.
components.detail: Drawn on a full-size 2D canvas placed behind the map canvas by a custom layer's render hook (`skyDraw`), projecting directions 'at infinity' with the map's camera, so the earth hides whatever lies behind it. Pictures and star data come from sky/ (precached with the app). The sun and moon appear only with day and night on; each can be switched off and sized.

mem: full-screen canvas + sun sprite canvases (est. 15-40 MB)
store: ~285 KB of sky files in the app cache
cpu: redrawn when the view or the time changes; star positions by one matrix (v347)

components.name: Sky behind the map
components.desc: Paints a sky behind the globe and tilted views - Flammarion-style blue with stars, zodiac lines, the sun and the moon where they truly stand from the place shown.
components.detail: `skyHook` adds an empty custom layer `skybodies` whose render callback runs `skyDraw` every map frame; frames where view, time and settings are unchanged are skipped (v347). `skyDraw` keeps a full-size canvas `#skyBg` behind the map canvas (so the earth hides what lies behind it), fills a blue gradient, projects each sky direction 'at infinity' with the map's own camera matrix (`mat4v`, `skyDir`), turns the stars with sidereal time, and - with sunlight on - draws the sun (coloured by its height above the visible horizon, `sunSeen`) and the moon (phase, lit side towards the sun), both kept upright relative to the earth's centre. Sizes follow the setting skySize (1-24).

mem: a full-screen 2D canvas at device pixel ratio (est. 8-30 MB)
store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: per map frame while the view or time changes: one matrix for all ~1,600 stars (a dozen multiplications each, v347); unchanged frames are skipped
gpu: a full-screen canvas composited behind the map

components.name: Moon drawing
components.desc: Draws the moon in its real phase: a crescent with an engraved face in profile, or the cream face cut by the terminator when more is lit.
components.detail: `moonProfile` draws the crescent from `MOON_PROF` (a profile outline joined by Catmull-Rom curves in `moonProfPath`) with rim hatching, brow, eye, nose, mouth and chin; for a lit fraction of 35 % or more `skyDraw` clips `sky/moonface.webp` to an ellipse terminator instead. The dark side is deep blue with a crown of short strokes around the bright limb.

components.name: Stars and zodiac lines
components.desc: Real stars down to the 5th magnitude drawn as yellow six-pointed engraving stars, and the twelve zodiac constellations joined by fine silver lines.
components.detail: `skyStars` fetches `sky/stars.json` once (1,627 Hipparcos stars via d3-celestial: RA, Dec, magnitude, HIP) and precomputes size by magnitude plus a seeded random rotation and ray jitter; the brightest get a crown of rays. `skyZodiac` fetches `sky/zodiac.json` (29 polylines). `skyStar` draws one star outline in yellow with a black edge. Both repaint the map when loaded and retry if the fetch failed.

store: ~45 KB data in the app cache
cpu: stars projected by one combined matrix (v347); only those on screen are drawn

components.name: Sun sprite and colours
components.desc: The engraved sun face, coloured by its height: red, rose and gold when rising; gold, orange and crimson when setting.
components.detail: `skyImg` loads the sprites (`sky/sun.webp` 600 px, `sky/moonface.webp`) once and repaints when ready. `sunTint` interpolates RGB along `SUN_RISE`/`SUN_SET` (true altitude, used with an obelisk) or `SUN_RISE_V`/`SUN_SET_V` (height above the horizon the camera sees). `skySunTinted` splits the sprite once into 'paper' and 'ink' canvases, then composes a tinted copy per (quantised) colour, keeping the last 6.

mem: 600 × 600 sprite split into canvases plus up to 6 tinted copies (~1.4 MB each, est. ~12 MB)
store: sun.webp ~230 KB in the app cache
cpu: per-pixel split once; a new tint when the colour changes

components.name: Day and night
components.desc: Day and night on the map: the night side darkened through twilight, the relief and the globe's atmosphere lit from where the sun really stands, with the time running live, animated over a day or a year, or set by hand.
components.detail: Sun and moon positions are computed in the app (`sunPos`, `moonPos`, `sunAt`) without any network. `sunApply` pushes the current sun into the map's light, the patched hillshade shader (`self.__pultSun`), the 512 × 256 night canvas, the sundial, the obelisk and the sky. `sunClock` drives the time: every 30 s for Now, or a frame loop applying about 20 times a second for Animate and Year. Settings live in the map config (mapCfg).

cpu: while animating: full sun update ~20×/s on the main thread
gpu: night raster layer and map repaints

components.name: Clock and animation
components.desc: Runs the sun's time: real time ('Now'), days running fast ('Animate'), the year running ('Year'), or set by hand.
components.detail: `sunOn` and `sunTime` read the switch and the current sun time (`M.sunT`). `sunClock` stops the previous timer and starts the mode: Now updates every 30 s; Animate advances time by `sunSpeed` seconds per day in a requestAnimationFrame loop and applies at most every 50 ms; Year advances whole days (keeping the hour) so a year takes `sunYear` seconds, pausing while the dial is dragged. `sunSet` saves settings and, when the sun is switched, rebuilds the map style.

components.name: Places in texts
components.desc: Finds the place names in any text by looking up the lemmas of proper nouns in the gazetteer, picks the most likely place, and lets the reader correct it.

cpu: scanning a text and scoring candidates, after each text is opened

components.name: Choosing the place
components.desc: Decides which of several same-named places a word means, and how sure that is.
components.detail: `choosePlaces` applies the reader's corrections first (`pl|`, `plw|`, `plg|` settings), drops places first attested clearly after the work's date (`workYear`: the reader's date or the author's from the catalogue), then scores candidates by closeness to the unambiguous places nearby in the text and to the text's 'home region', by fame (names, city, rank) and by the cue word. A result is marked uncertain as 'later', 'person', 'ambiguous' or 'form' (stem only). `dictSaysPerson` reads the beginning of the dictionary entries for the name and counts whether most call it a person or a place. `textKeyOf`/`workKeyOf` give the keys under which corrections are stored.

cpu: per text; dictionary look-ups per name

components.name: Correcting places
components.desc: Lets the reader confirm, change or remove the place of a word, for one passage, the work, or everywhere.
components.detail: The card's 'change' panel (`changeHTML`) lists other places of the same name with their distance, a gazetteer search, 'Pick on the map …' (a new own place) and 'Back to the automatic choice'. `saveCorrection` stores the choice under `pl|text|word`, `plw|work|name` or `plg|name`, re-runs the recognition, and offers to apply the same to the other passages of that name. `checkPop` lists all uncertain places of the part ('⚑ n to check') with one-tap confirm or reject; `UNSURE` holds the reasons shown.

components.name: Finding names
components.desc: Picks out the words of a text that may name a place and their candidate places.
components.detail: `findPlaceHits` goes through the tokens, keeps capitalised words, and skips words analysed as ordinary words, adjectives, verbs, Roman numerals and sentence-initial function words (`FUNC_WORDS`). It reads all name bundles the text may need at once, then `placeCands` looks up the exact key (and, for unanalysed words, the stem key, main places only), at most 40 candidates. Neighbouring words give hints: 'flumen', 'urbs', 'ποταμός' say what kind of place (`CUES`); 'filia', 'uxor' or titles like 'Caesar', 'rex' next to it say it is a person (`PERSON_CUES`, `TITLE_CUES`). `plainName` strips vowel-length marks from Latin names.

components.detail: `mapManifest` (maps.js) reads it with a 6 s limit and stores a copy in the cache 'pult-maps'; the service worker also answers it network-first from that copy. Each entry names the site its files come from (`url`: the lesepult-maps site), so only this small list lives on the app's own site.

The revision view (librev.js) downloads a work again to compare versions. HEAD requests on the catalogue serve as the online check.

The private packages.json is merged into the public manifest, so private packages appear and update like the others. The service worker never caches these cross-origin requests.

components.name: Offline helper
components.desc: The service worker: keeps the app and its data on the device and serves them without a network.

components.name: Install as an app (web manifest)
components.desc: Lets Pult be added to the home screen and run full-screen like an app, with its name, colours and icon.
components.detail: manifest.webmanifest: name and short name "Pult", start URL and scope "./", display standalone, dark background #1b1a18 and theme #2a2926, icons 192 and 512 px (index.html adds a 180 px apple-touch-icon). Only an installed (home screen) Pult usually gets persistent storage, which is why This Pult advises starting from the icon.

components.name: Request routing
components.desc: Decides for every request of the page whether it is answered from the device, from the network, or first one and then the other.
components.detail: One fetch handler with rules in order: Mapterhorn tiles → saved relief; other sites → not touched; other paths on the same host (lesepult-maps) → network; packages/ and texts/ → network (stored in IndexedDB by the app); lib/ → long-term library cache; maps/maps.json → network then copy; maps/ → map package cache; everything else → network first with a time limit, cached copy when offline.

components.name: App files: network first, cache when offline
components.desc: Pages, scripts, styles and fonts come fresh from the website when it answers quickly, otherwise from the stored copy — so updates arrive at once and offline still works.
components.detail: The top-level code holds the install, activate and fetch listeners. For app files the fetch handler uses `net()` (fetch with `cache: 'no-cache'` and an abort after 4 s for pages, 8 s for files, because iOS often lets offline requests hang), stores each good answer back into the app cache, and on failure serves the cached copy (ignoring query strings; a navigation falls back to `./` or index.html), and as a last resort tries the network once more without a limit. `clean()` re-wraps redirected responses because Safari refuses redirected pages from a service worker (GitHub Pages redirects /lesepult → /lesepult/).
components.netNote: online: up to 4-8 s wait before falling back when the network is slow

store: lesepult-vNNN, refreshed on every online load

components.name: Never cached
components.desc: Downloads of dictionary packages and library texts, other websites (GitHub API, imagery, Nominatim) and the map-package site go straight to the network.
components.detail: The handler returns without answering for non-GET requests, foreign origins (e.g. the private repository via api.github.com), same-host paths outside the app scope (j555g.github.io/lesepult-maps/) and paths containing `/packages/` or `/texts/`. Those downloads are stored by the app itself in IndexedDB or the map cache, so a second copy in the service-worker cache would only waste space.

components.name: Large libraries: cache first
components.desc: Large libraries under lib/ (three.js, versioned in the file name) are fetched once and then always served from their own cache, across app updates.
components.detail: Only the app's own `lib/` folder (three.js) is answered from `pult-lib`, or fetched once and stored, and kept across app updates. Until v347 the rule matched any path containing `/lib/`, so the map package's `maps/base/lib/pmtiles.js` came from the app site instead of the downloaded package and could be missing offline; fixed in v347.
components.netNote: first use needs the network, afterwards offline

components.name: Map packages and list
components.desc: Map files are served from the downloaded packages; the list of map packages always comes fresh from the network when possible.
components.detail: `maps/maps.json` is fetched with a 6 s limit and falls back to the copy maps.js stores in `pult-maps`. Other `maps/` requests (GeoJSON layers, engine CSS/JS from base/lib5) are answered from `pult-maps` by URL without query, otherwise from the network (the app site's own maps/ copy). PMTiles packages are not requested through here: maps.js reads them straight from the cache.
components.netNote: installed packages offline; maps.json and missing files online

mem: one response (large GeoJSON up to ~3.7 MB)
store: reads pult-maps (up to ~95 MB of current packages)

components.name: Relief tiles: saved areas first
components.desc: Elevation tiles from Mapterhorn are handed to the saved-relief code, which answers from the saved areas first.
components.detail: Requests to `tiles.mapterhorn.com` go to `reliefServe()` from reliefsw.js (owned by the relief part of the map): saved tile from `pult-relief`, otherwise the network, offline an enlarged tile from a coarser saved one.
components.netNote: saved areas offline; everything else online

cpu: routing only; enlarging is in map.relief

components.name: Service worker install and update
components.desc: Stores the app's own files on the device when a new version is installed, and clears caches of older versions.
components.detail: sw.js is registered by the app shell; it pulls in reliefsw.js (saved relief) with `importScripts`. A new version is a new cache name `lesepult-vNNN`; the new worker takes over at once (`skipWaiting`, `clients.claim`).

components.name: Old caches removed
components.desc: When a new version activates, caches of older versions are deleted; map packages, saved relief and large libraries are kept.
components.detail: The activate handler (in the top-level code) deletes every cache except the current `lesepult-vNNN`, `pult-maps`, `pult-relief` and `pult-lib`. Note: `pult-dl-parts` is not in that keep list, so parts of an interrupted map download are dropped whenever the app updates (the download then starts over).

store: frees old app caches (~2.7 MB each)

components.name: App files kept offline
components.desc: On install, every script, the stylesheet, fonts, icons and sky pictures (about 2.7 MB) are fetched fresh and stored, so Pult starts without a network.
components.detail: `FILES` lists 54 entries (all app scripts, style.css, fonts.css, manifest, the three icons, sky/sun.webp, moonface.webp, zodiac.json, stars.json, Roboto Condensed, Source Sans 3 and Gentium Book Plus subsets) under `CACHE` ('lesepult-v346'). Each is fetched with `cache: 'reload'`; any failure aborts the install, so a half-stored version never takes over. The four Gentium 700-italic files are not listed (fonts.css does not use them).
components.netNote: filled online at install, used offline

components.name: Reader
components.desc: Shows a text word by word, analyses each word and colours it by grammar.

components.name: Word-class colours
components.desc: Colours each word by its word class (noun, verb, participle, particle …), with colours you can change.
components.detail: Fifteen classes with default colours (`POS`); the class of each word comes from its reading, treebank hints and the lemma. Colours are applied by an injected style sheet keyed on the `p-<class>` class of each word, so changing a colour needs no redraw.

components.name: Colour buttons
components.desc: The buttons in Settings → Colourisation that switch classes and show their colours.
components.detail: `COL_GROUPS` adds punctuation to the grammar groups; `chipGroupsHTML` builds the grouped buttons for both the colour and the grammar settings; `syncPosRows` updates their state and colours. Holding a button opens the palette (in `wire`).

components.name: Word classes
components.desc: The list of word classes with their names and default colours.
components.detail: `POS` holds id, label and default colour for 15 classes (incl. punctuation marks); `posLab` gives a label, `posOnOf` whether a class is coloured.

components.name: Finding the word class
components.desc: Decides the word class of a word from its lemma and reading.
components.detail: `posOf` checks the article and a list of Greek `PARTICLES`, then the analysis (participle, infinitive, finite verb), capitalised lemmas (proper nouns), the treebank class of the lemma (`S.lemmapos` / Latin `S.latPos`, mapped by `UPOS2`), indeclinable tags and finally case endings.

components.name: Applying the colours
components.desc: Switches the colouring on or off and applies the chosen colours.
components.detail: `applyPosColors` writes `<style id="posStyle">` with one rule per coloured class (and punctuation), toggles `body.pos` and the Colours button.

components.name: Interlinear glosses
components.desc: Your own translations written under words or phrases, plus a default gloss per lemma used everywhere it appears.
components.detail: A gloss belongs to a span of words in one text (`glosses` store); a default gloss belongs to a lemma (`lg|<lemma>` in settings) and is shown wherever that lemma occurs, either only where there is no own gloss or always (gloss mode "both"). Glosses are edited in the gloss box at the top of the dictionary pane or added from a selection in a dictionary entry.

store: glosses store + lg| settings, est. KB to a few MB
cpu: saving a gloss redraws the text

components.name: Adding glosses
components.desc: Adds selected dictionary text as a gloss or a default gloss.
components.detail: `addGloss(text, asDefault, add)` checks that a text and word (or a lemma) is selected, appends or replaces, records the lemma name (`lemmaNameSet`) for default glosses, redraws and confirms with a notice. `writeGloss` and `editGloss` are older dialog-based editors that nothing in the current code calls.

components.name: Gloss box
components.desc: The two editable fields at the top of the dictionary pane: the gloss of the tapped word or phrase and the default gloss of its lemma.
components.detail: `fillGlossBox` writes the two textareas for the current selection and lemma, but leaves them alone while one is being edited; `autoGrow` sizes them to their content. `openGlossField` makes sure the word is shown in the dictionary pane (`showWord`) and puts the cursor at the end of the requested field. Saving happens on change in `wire` (Enter finishes, Shift+Enter adds a line).

components.name: Gloss display
components.desc: How glosses appear under the words: blue, small, wider when long, never wider than the text column.
components.detail: `glossHTML` escapes a gloss and keeps its line breaks; `dgHTML` renders a lemma's default gloss; `glW` widens a gloss longer than 70 characters in proportion (`--gw`), and `setGlossMax` caps it at 80 % of the text width (`--glmax`), re-run by a ResizeObserver on the text body.

components.name: Saving glosses
components.desc: Creates, changes and deletes glosses and default glosses.
components.detail: `saveSpanGloss` creates, updates or (for empty text) deletes the gloss of a word or phrase, stamping it with its words and context via `glossStamp` so it can be re-attached after a text revision. `setDefaultGloss` sets or removes a lemma's default gloss; `cleanGloss` tidies spaces but keeps typed line breaks; `joinGloss` appends with "; " unless already present; `spanGloss` finds a gloss; `targetLemma` gives the lemma of the selected word as chosen in the dictionary pane.

components.name: Grammar line
components.desc: The small line under each word with its grammatical form, e.g. "masc/neut gen sg", configurable per word class.
components.detail: The text comes from the chosen analysis, compressed when several readings differ in only one feature; indeclinable words show their word class. Which word classes show the line is a setting (`gramCfg`), applied by an injected style sheet so no redraw is needed.

components.name: Grammar line buttons
components.desc: The word-class buttons in Settings → Grammar line.
components.detail: `gramRowsHTML` builds the grouped buttons, `syncGramRows` updates their pressed state; `gramDialog`, an older stand-alone dialog, is not called anywhere now.

components.name: Which classes show it
components.desc: Chooses for which word classes the grammar line is shown.
components.detail: `GRAM_GROUPS` sorts the classes into Inflected words, Verb forms and Indeclinable and other; `GRAM_DEF` / `defaultGramCfg` show all but numerals, conjunctions, particles and other; `allGramCfg` shows all. `applyGramCfg` writes a `<style id="gramStyle">` that hides the line for switched-off classes.

components.name: Grammar line text
components.desc: Turns analyses into the short line shown under a word.
components.detail: `gramText` strips dialect and clitic notes, and if several analyses differ in one position only, joins them ("nom/voc/abl sg"); otherwise it shows the first and "(+n)". `indeclClass` names the class of words that do not inflect, preferring the treebank's class for this passage (`CTX_POS`), then the analysis (`INDECL_RE`), then the lemma's usual class (`INDECL_LAB`), and handles Latin enclitics ("indecl + -que").

components.name: Morphology and dictionary lookup
components.desc: Finds the possible lemmas and grammatical analyses of a Greek or Latin form, and the dictionary entries for a key.
components.detail: Greek forms are looked up in the installed morphology package (a big form → analyses table split into buckets); Latin forms are analysed by a small engine that combines stems and endings (Collatinus or Whitaker's Words data). Dictionary and morphology data are read bucket by bucket from IndexedDB with a 300-bucket memory cache.

mem: bucket cache (≤300 buckets, ~10 KB each in JSON, est. 3-10 MB) plus the Latin engine (est. 20-40 MB when loaded)
cpu: per lookup; Latin analysis is pure computation

components.name: Bucket reading and cache
components.desc: Fetches the piece ("bucket") of a dictionary or morphology database that holds a given key.
components.detail: `bucketOf` maps a key to its bucket name exactly like the toolkit's `bucket_of()` (a 3-letter prefix, longer where a prefix was split). `bucket` reads it from the dictionary's database and keeps it in `bucketCache`, a Map that drops the oldest entry beyond 300.

mem: up to 300 buckets (~10-12 KB JSON each on average, some > 100 KB), est. 3-10 MB

components.name: Finding dictionary entries
components.desc: Gives the dictionary pane the entries of all switched-on dictionaries for a lemma key.
components.detail: `entriesFor(key, lang)` reads the key's bucket in each shown dictionary of that language and returns matching entries in order, plus morphology cross-references (`#m`); `entryByRef` fetches one entry by key and id. Used by the dictionary pane and the map.

components.name: Greek analysis
components.desc: Lists the lemmas and analyses of a Greek form and which lemma is preferred.
components.detail: `analyses(form)` canonicalises the form, finds it in its morphology bucket (also without a second enclitic accent), groups the analyses by lemma and picks a lemma: your ★ choice, else the package's or the hints' preference (`morphPref`), else the first. Latin forms are passed on to `latAnalyses`. It is used by the dictionary, search, glosses, Library and maps as well.

components.name: Latin analysis engine
components.desc: Analyses Latin forms by splitting them into stem and ending, as Collatinus or Whitaker's Words do.
components.detail: `latEngine` loads the installed engine (the single `engine` record of the chosen package) once into memory and derives Latin word classes (`S.latPos`). `latAnalyze` tries every stem/ending split (`latAnalyzeKeyC` for Collatinus, `wwAnalyzeKey` + `wwFits` for Whitaker), plus contracted perfects, assimilated prefixes (adc-/acc-) and the enclitics -que/-ne/-ve. `latAnalyses` groups the results by lemma and puts the most frequent lemma first (`latFreq`).

mem: the whole engine as one object: Collatinus ~7.6 MB / Whitaker ~2.7 MB of JSON, est. 20-40 MB in memory
cpu: loading the engine once; then string work per form

components.name: Latin vowel lengths
components.desc: Puts macrons and breves on Latin words (rŏsā) when "vowel lengths" is on.
components.detail: `quantify` transfers the marks of the analysed spelling onto the form as written, keeping its case and i/j, u/v, or gives up if the letters do not match; `qCommon` keeps only the marks all readings agree on. Whitaker's data has no lengths, so `colEngine` loads the Collatinus engine as well and `qFromCol` takes the lengths of the closest Collatinus analysis of the same lemma (`QTOK`, `CONS`).

mem: a second Latin engine when Whitaker is used, est. 20 MB

components.name: Opening a text and keeping your place
components.desc: Loads a text or library book, splits it into words, and keeps the reading position and your bookmark.
